clusters.architecture_notes: config.py (2815 lines, 21.2% prose) does several jobs in one file. It defines the scenario grammar's dataclasses (distribution specs, the *DistributionConfig family, ScenarioConfig, SimulationPeriod, OutputConfig, ParameterSweepConfig), plus GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig, which BatteryConfig holds. It also holds the block readers, the fleet sampler, the file loaders, YAML variable substitution, a parameter-sweep runner that calls simulate_home and simulate_fleet, and the community readers. The shared boundary mechanism is small: _refuse_unrecognised_keys and _require_mapping for key sets, _child_path for error paths, and _BlockType for blocks with a `type:` key. Under it there is no field-level reader. Each parse_* function settles coercion, defaults and refusal wording in one of three ways. It may splat the raw YAML mapping into the domain dataclass (_parse_pv_config, _parse_battery_config, _parse_load_config, _parse_grid_charge_config). It may call float(), int() or str() inline with the default restated (_parse_heat_pump_config, _parse_ev_config, the distribution builders, parse_fleet_distribution_config). Or it may use a coercion table built on _number (parse_finance_config, _parse_grid_services_events_config). Domain constraints live in the __post_init__ of each component dataclass, in pv.py, battery.py, load.py, heat_pump.py, ev.py and location.py. Those raise ValueError with no block path and do no type, bool or NaN checks of their own. GridChargeConfig, DispatchStrategyConfig, FinanceConfig and FleetDistributionConfig raise ConfigurationError instead. Each component's field list is restated in up to seven places: the domain dataclass, the _X_BLOCK_KEYS set, the scenario_writer block, the *DistributionConfig, the distribution parser's .get defaults, generate_homes_from_distribution's `else <default>` fallbacks, and the _modify_* sweep rebuilders. The scenario document's shape (scenario list, single scenario, home file, fleet homes, fleet distribution, sweep) is classified by checking which top-level keys are present. That check happens separately in config.py's loaders, cli/validate.py, cli/home.py via cli/utils.load_config_with_overrides, cli/fleet.py and web/fleet_scenario.py. scenario_writer.py is a hand-maintained inverse of the block readers. Only CLAUDE.md prose and a round-trip test whose fixture lists fields by hand keep the two in step. The web layer has the typed readers config.py lacks: web/number_fields.as_finite_float and as_whole_number, built on whole_numbers.whole_number.

clusters.diagnosis: config.py reads 51 numeric values in three styles: raw splat into the domain dataclass, inline float() or int(), or the _number coercion table. None of them enforces the rule that a number is finite, never a bool, whole where it is a count, and refused with its key path (fk-649851e5fc38). The domain constructors that receive the splatted values check bounds only. They raise without the block path the reader holds, and some errors escape as TypeError (fk-e2aaf2bfe651). Each component's fields and defaults are written up to four times: in the dataclass, the *DistributionConfig, its parser's data.get fallbacks, and generate_homes_from_distribution (fk-148991ab9439). scenario_writer.py is a second grammar kept in step by hand, and it already loses PVConfig.system_losses on a round trip (fk-2b16cc8bcf46). Which kind of document a file is gets decided by key-presence tests in five or more places. `home run` edits the raw dict before parsing, so a flat 9 kW home runs as 4 kW (fk-2264bc150fa3). run_parameter_sweep and the _modify_* copy-constructors have no production caller, yet live tasks 237 and 320 are repairing them (fk-59fdc80fdded). ConfigurationError and the two battery-domain config types sit in the top module. finance, gridservices and battery therefore reach back with eleven deferred imports and TYPE_CHECKING imports (fk-4435376bedb3). The heuristic-14 measurement of config.py names the fleet-distribution grammar and sampler as the first partition. It can move only after the error type and the number primitives sit below it (fk-2dc9d1cd2c06). The commits arrive as TDD triples, but the recurrence is real: one defect class, fixed one reader at a time.

clusters.architecture_notes: The dashboard has three request-body grammars that end in config.py's scenario grammar or in HomeConfig. (1) The single-home page posts a flat body (pv_kw, battery_kwh, efficiency_pct, ...). simulation_params.parse_home_config builds HomeConfig directly with its own defaults table (_HOME_CONFIG_DEFAULTS) and its own heat_pump sub-grammar. It delegates only tariff, dispatch and seg to config's parsers. (2) The fleet page posts a nested body that fleet_config.form_to_fleet_distribution_config walks and rebuilds into config's fleet_distribution dict, pre-reading every number through number_fields. fleet_scenario.parse_fleet_form then hands it to config.parse_fleet_distribution_config and generate_homes_from_distribution and applies the tariff/dispatch/SEG overlay. (3) The scenario builder posts a flat, prefixed body (pv_distribution_type, pv_mean, pv_wd_values, ...). builder_form.scenario_from_builder_form translates it into a scenario document and validates it by writing YAML to a tempfile for load_fleet_config. Both fleet pages edit components through one editor state, FleetComponent/EditorDistribution plus distribution-editor.js, but each page serialises that state differently and has its own server decoder. The reverse direction is also split: the fleet page imports scenarios on the server (fleet_scenario.fleet_form_from_scenario, with a not_loaded list), while the builder imports them in the browser with js-yaml (scenario-builder.js scenarioFormFields). The distribution preview samples through fleet_config._draw_samples, not config's sampler. number_fields (as_finite_float, as_whole_number[_within]) is the one web number rule, but each endpoint must remember to call it, because config.py's own builders read numbers with bare float()/int(). Bounds reach page scripts through ad-hoc channels: the builder gets scenarios._script_components and the home page gets consumptionRange via tojson. The fleet and sweep scripts get nothing and hold literals. Tests drive public seams; no private-name patching was found.

clusters.cross_system_notes: scenario-config (src/solar_challenge/config.py) is the upstream subsystem behind most of this cluster's patching. (4) ShuffledPoolDistribution has no bound on its pool size relative to n_homes, so each web route must bound counts itself, and the builder route does not. Fixing (1) and (4) in config would delete compensations in web/fleet_config.py, web/fleet_scenario.py and web/builder_form.py.

clusters.architecture_notes: JobManager (web/jobs.py) is a per-app ThreadPoolExecutor wrapper. It holds each job's live state as a frozen JobState inside a mutable _TrackedJob, together with a 100-slot event deque and a finished_at stamp. It also mirrors every transition into SQLite's jobs table and partly into the runs table, using its own SQL and per-job connections (_record_new_job, _update_progress, _record_completed_job, _record_failed_job_row/_record_failed_run_row, _forget_job, recover_stale_jobs). Status values are typed Literals with CHECK constraints in database.py (JobStatus, RunStatus, RunType), so heuristic 12 is mostly met at the value level. The transitions themselves have no owner: any JobManager method can _report_state any status, and terminality comes from _run_job's try/except, not from the executor boundary (_finish_job only stamps finished_at). RunStorage (storage.py) owns the run files and a RunRecord-derived upsert, but the runs table is also written by jobs.py and read with raw SQL by api.history_list_runs, routes._get_aggregate_stats and assistant.list_recent_runs. A run's summary crosses every seam as an untyped JSON dict (RunRecord.decoded_summary returns Any), and each reader guesses home-run keys. The progress stream works like this: JobManager queues JobEvent(type, state); api.get_job_progress drains the deque and serializes per-type field subsets via _job_event_payload, plus three hand-written frames (timeout, not-found, late-complete). Two JS consumers parse it independently (progress-tracker.js, parameter-sweep.js._followPoint). The server names its failure event 'error', the same name as EventSource's native transport-error event. Each submit call carries db_path/data_dir, so the manager builds a fresh RunStorage per job instead of owning the app's one. create_app's atexit.register(job_manager.shutdown) holds a strong reference, so the module-level WeakSet registry (_active_managers, used by cli/web.py's shutdown_all_managers and the test drain) never actually drops an app's manager. The briefing's single-process, in-memory JobManager is by design and is not flagged.

clusters.root_cause: Three things each lack one owner and one typed contract. The job lifecycle has no transition table (fk-484952247bb6). The progress stream has no shared frame schema (fk-7eb56fda0b1c). The stored-run summary is an untyped dict (fk-a37ed16d59c5).
clusters.diagnosis: A job's state is four separately written facts: JobState.status, _TrackedJob.finished_at, the jobs row and the runs row. No legal-transition table governs them. A job becomes terminal in _run_job's try, not at the executor boundary, so an exception raised before that try leaves a finished job marked running (fk-484952247bb6). Nothing reads the jobs table; it is a write-only mirror, and maintaining it caused tasks 543 and 627 (fk-c14c02dc1b77). The runs table has writers and readers outside RunStorage (fk-9d7f66fdcfdd). The progress stream has one producer and two JS consumers, with no shared wire contract. Each event type carries a different field subset, three frames are built by hand, and the server's 'error' event collides with EventSource's transport error. A dropped connection therefore marks a running job failed (fk-7eb56fda0b1c). get_events drains a single-consumer deque, but a job's stream has several subscribers (fk-4540d657bff6). A stored run's summary crosses every seam as Any. Six readers guess home-run keys, so fleet runs read as null or zero (fk-a37ed16d59c5). Request fields are coerced per endpoint with silent defaults (fk-239274130a5a, weakened: the outer-object rule is shared). resolve_location silently turns any unrecognised location into Bristol (fk-acdc650baeb8). Docstring amends and mechanical sweeps inflate the counts, but the lifecycle and summary families are bug-driven.
clusters.exoneration_summary: Partial. Docstring and naming amends and three mechanical lint/type sweeps inflate the counts. The job-lifecycle, progress-stream and run-summary families are bug-driven.

clusters.architecture_notes: home.py::simulate_home is the one composition point. It fetches the TMY, builds PV, calls load.generate_load_profile (which folds EV load in itself), folds heat-pump load in inline, builds a stateful battery.py::Battery, picks one of two dispatch mechanisms and runs a per-minute loop of flow.simulate_timestep or flow.simulate_timestep_tou, then prices the flows. The Strategy family (dispatch.py::DispatchStrategy and its three subclasses) is a one-shot decide_action(timestamp, gen_kw, dem_kw, soc_kwh, capacity_kwh, minutes, grid_charge_ctx) returning a DispatchDecision. flow.simulate_timestep then executes that decision against the Battery. flow.simulate_timestep_tou is the rate-aware path: it decides and executes inline, interleaved with battery.charge calls. Battery is the only owner of the derived SOC envelope: SOH resolution, effective_capacity_kwh, and min/max_soc_kwh from overridable fractions held in the frozen _SocLimitsAndEfficiencies. BatteryConfig only knows nominal capacity and config fractions. EnergyFlowResult is a mutable per-step record whose derived flows (export, import, self-consumption) the callers compute. validate_energy_balance re-checks six of its fields afterwards, and callers can turn that check off. Dispatch selection is two string fields: HomeConfig.dispatch_strategy ('greedy'/'tou_optimized', not validated) and BatteryConfig.dispatch_strategy.strategy_type ('self_consumption'/'tou_optimized'/'peak_shaving'). home.py routes them with if/elif plus a use_tariff_tou precedence flag. fleet.py fans simulate_home out to processes and sums series by attribute-name strings. community.py replays fleet aggregates through simulate_timestep with a hard-coded SelfConsumptionStrategy, which the briefing records as known. Each module validates its numeric inputs with its own inline comparisons. clusters.architecture_notes: The lock is three layers. src/solar_challenge/__init__.py declares the 69 public names three times (a literal __all__, _SYMBOL_MODULE, and a TYPE_CHECKING import block), plus _SOURCE_NAME for the one alias, and resolves them lazily through PEP-562 __getattr__. tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py holds three hand-pasted text tables: FROZEN_SURFACE (name to form), FROZEN_CLOSURE (classes outside __all__ that the surface names) and FROZEN_MEMBERS (public members per pinned class). Each test recomputes the current form of every name and diffs it against its table. The forms come from tests/_surface_forms.py, which exposes six public functions: surface_form, member_forms, named_classes, signature_closure, undeclared_attributes and unset_attributes. Its engine is _parsed, which turns a runtime annotation into a small frozen _Construct tree (_Leaf, _Union, _Subscripted, _Declared, _Unevaluated and others). Each construct has a text() spelling, meant to read the same on every Python minor, and a classes(module) method that feeds the closure walk. Anything _parsed has no rule for raises TypeError, which is the fail-closed behaviour of task 602. Strings are spelled as written but evaluated in their module's globals, plus the imports of its top-level `if TYPE_CHECKING:` blocks, to find classes. For a dataclass-generated __init__, _spelling_modules finds the module for each parameter by walking the MRO. Members are read from each class's own body, plus an ast scan of its source for attributes set on self. tests/unit/test_surface_forms_helper.py (94 tests) drives only the six public functions and builds fixtures through importable modules, so it does not pin internals. tests/unit/test_surface_forms_type_check.py runs mypy on the helper. findings.title: Web layer rebuilds config's distribution grammar to compensate for config's missing number invariant, and the rebuild silently drops keys
findings.statement: config.py's distribution grammar reads numbers with bare float()/int(). config.py::_build_normal_spec calls float(data['mean']), _build_weighted_discrete_spec calls float(w), and _build_shuffled_pool_spec calls int(c), which truncates 2.5 and raises OverflowError on inf. parse_fleet_distribution_config truncates n_homes with int() and takes seed unchecked. NormalDistribution, UniformDistribution and ShuffledPoolDistribution.__post_init__ check ordering and sign but not finiteness. Because of this, every web entry point must pre-read every number through number_fields before config sees it. To reach those numbers, fleet_config.py::_parse_component_distribution walks and rebuilds each block through _build_distribution_dict and _other_setting. The rebuild is lossy and re-decides what config already decides; all of the following was run at the pin: (a) pv.capacity_kw {type: normal, mena: 4, std: 1} becomes {type: normal, mean: 0.0, std: 1.0}, and config accepts N(0,1), because the misspelt key never reaches config's _refuse_unrecognised_keys. (b) pv.tilt {type: fixed, value: 30} and battery.max_charge_kw {type: proportional_to, source: battery.capacity_kwh, multiplier: 0.5} are both valid in config's grammar, but they are cut down to {type: ...} and refused with "requires 'value'" or "requires 'source'", naming a key the user did send. (c) _spec_number invents defaults that config's grammar refuses as missing: mean 0, std 1, uniform 0..1, weight 1, count 1. fleet_scenario::_read_fleet_size_and_seed exists only to run 'ahead of the loaders, whose int() would refuse n_homes first'. Each new entry point repeats the pre-read or forgets it: api.py::simulate_sweep still uses bare float()/int(), and assistant.py reads n_homes with int().
findings.proposal: Give the number invariant one home in config.py. Add _finite_number(value, path) and _whole_count(value, path, low=0), built on whole_numbers.whole_number; they refuse bool, NaN, inf and fractions with a ConfigurationError naming the path. Call them from every _build_*_spec, from _parse_distribution_spec's scalar branch, and from parse_fleet_distribution_config for n_homes and seed. Repeat the finiteness check in the __post_init__ of NormalDistribution, UniformDistribution, WeightedDiscreteDistribution and ShuffledPoolDistribution, so it is enforced at both construction and parse (heuristic 10, redundant). This refuses NaN for the downstream consumer too, which is intended. Apply the dashboard-only bounds (MAX_FLEET_HOMES on n_homes and on pool totals) once, to the parsed FleetDistributionConfig, not to the raw dict. The web layer can then pass blocks through as sent, so config's unrecognised-key and presence rules see what the user posted. What becomes deletable: fleet_config._other_setting, _spec_number and the _is_fixed_value branch of _parse_component_distribution; the read_fleet_size/read_fleet_seed pre-reads; fleet_scenario._read_fleet_size_and_seed's ordering hack; and FLEET_FORM_REFUSALS' need to list ValueError. This would have prevented 312, 441, 498, 520, the 509 class of dropped or ignored keys, and the strip bugs that 519 and 535 patched one shape at a time.

Not independently checked: the api.py::simulate_sweep and assistant.py parts.

findings.title: One editor distribution, two wire encodings, two server decoders with different defaults and bounds
findings.statement: Both fleet pages edit a component through one editor state, fleet_components.py::EditorDistribution.editor_state and distribution-editor.js, but each page serialises it into its own wire grammar. fleet-simulator.js _buildDistPayload posts a nested body: {pv: {capacity_kw: {type, mean, ..., values: [{value, weight}], entries: [{value, count}]}}}. scenario-builder.js componentFormData flattens the same state to pv_distribution_type, pv_mean, pv_wd_values and pv_sp_entries. Two server decoders then turn these into config's grammar under different rules. fleet_config.py::_build_distribution_dict defaults absent parameters, bounds pool counts by MAX_FLEET_HOMES through _pool_counts, and returns a bare {type} for a type it does not know. builder_form.py::_distribution_spec leaves absent parameters out for the loader to refuse, reads counts through as_whole_number with no bound, and refuses an unknown type itself. Verified at the pin: the builder's {type: normal, mean: 4} is refused by the loader ("requires 'mean' and 'std'"), while the fleet page's {type: normal} runs as N(0,1). The component keys are restated as well. FLEET_COMPONENTS already carries grammar_key, yet fleet_config::form_to_fleet_distribution_config and fleet_scenario::_read_fleet_distribution/_read_battery hard-code 'capacity_kw', 'capacity_kwh' and 'annual_consumption_kwh'. Every distribution rule is therefore decided twice on the server, and a third time in each page's JS.
findings.proposal: Make the editor state the one wire shape. A module web/editor_distribution.py, or methods on EditorDistribution, would provide three things. read_editor_distribution(obj, path) is the one reader of an editor dist's numbers and rows (finite floats, whole bounded counts). to_grammar_spec() returns config's spec, and from_grammar_spec(spec, path) is its inverse. Both pages post {component.key: <editor dist>} exactly as the editor holds it. Server loops iterate FLEET_COMPONENTS and use grammar_key, never literals. What becomes deletable: fleet-simulator.js::_buildDistPayload/_distFromConfig and scenario-builder.js::componentFormData; builder_form._DISTRIBUTION_FIELDS, _prefixed, _distribution_spec and _row_lists; fleet_config._build_distribution_dict, _named_rows, _spec_number and _pool_counts; and distribution_form_spec/_form_numbers/_form_number_list/_form_count_list, which become the module's inverse. This would have prevented 313 (two writers disagree), 553 and 561, the restated-keys half of 566 and 611, and the unbounded builder pool below.
findings.bug_history_link: live 313, 553, 611; done 561 (8938c5e, d7d15d7), 566 (4defa18), 278 (e128829, e55b645), 498 (a530806 fixed counts in fleet_config only)
findings.verdict_notes: Two decoders confirmed. fleet_config::_build_distribution_dict defaults absent params, bounds counts via _pool_counts, and returns a bare {type} for an unknown type. builder_form::_distribution_spec leaves params absent, reads counts through as_whole_number (no bound), and raises on an unknown type. Both fleet-simulator.js and scenario-builder.js exist. fleet_components.py builder_default values differ from the JS literals (max 15.0 vs 13.5, load 6000 vs 5000). I did not re-verify every hard-coded grammar key.

findings.title: Builder validate builds an unbounded shuffled pool: the 312 bound was applied to one decoder only
findings.statement: builder_form.py::_distribution_spec reads shuffled_pool counts with as_whole_number, which has no bound, and _dashboard_limit_errors checks no count. Verified at the pin: scenario_from_builder_form accepts {n_homes: 10, pv_distribution_type: shuffled_pool, pv_sp_entries: [{value: 4, count: 10**12}]}, and the dashboard limits report no error. builder_form_errors then runs load_fleet_config on that document, since n_homes is within bounds. The path continues through generate_homes_from_distribution and _DistributionSampler.prepare to ShuffledPoolDistribution.create_pool, which builds [4.0] * 10**12 inside the request thread of POST /api/scenarios/validate, exhausting memory. Commit de19110 (fix 312) says 'so no route builds an unbounded pool', but it bounded only fleet_config._pool_counts, which the builder route never reaches.
findings.proposal: Immediate fix: read builder counts through the same bounded rule, by sharing fleet_config._pool_counts or calling as_whole_number_within(count, field, 0, MAX_FLEET_HOMES) plus a total check, so validate refuses before load_fleet_config runs. Structural fix: the single editor-distribution decoder in the finding above. Also bound the pool total against n_homes in config itself, so no caller can build a pool larger than the fleet.
findings.bug_history_link: sibling of task 312 (de19110, fa13e98); not among the live tasks named in the brief
findings.verdict_notes: Ran builder_form_errors with a valid form and shuffled_pool count 10**9 under a 3GB address-space limit. It raised MemoryError from config.py::ShuffledPoolDistribution.create_pool via generate_homes_from_distribution, _DistributionSampler.prepare. No dashboard limit refuses the count; _dashboard_limit_errors checks only name, n_homes and fixed ranges. fleet_config._pool_counts bounds counts for the fleet route only. Real unbounded allocation; the 'request thread of POST /api/scenarios/validate' route detail was not traced.

findings.title: Sweep endpoint re-implements config.SweepSpec inline: unknown mode runs linear, steps unbounded, third copy of point generation in JS
findings.statement: api.py::simulate_sweep re-derives SweepSpec's validation and get_values inline. min, max and steps are read with bare float()/int(), so an infinite value is an OverflowError and a 500 (live task 440). Any mode string other than 'geometric' silently runs linear, whereas SweepSpec.__post_init__ refuses an unknown mode. steps has only a lower bound: steps=10**6 parses 10**6 HomeConfigs and submits 10**6 jobs (live task 140 asks for a Steps max). parameter-sweep.js previewValues is a third copy of the point generation. Its parameterOptions restate ranges that disagree with the server: PV 1-20 against parse_home_config's 0.5-20, consumption 1000-10000 against FLEET_COMPONENTS load 500-20000, and battery 0-50 against FLEET_COMPONENTS battery 0-100. The handler also has gratuitous function-local imports (uuid, math) that break no cycle.
findings.proposal: Add web/sweep_request.py::read_sweep_request(body) -> SweepRequest(parameter, home_key, spec: config.SweepSpec). It reads min and max with as_finite_float_within(parameter range), steps with as_whole_number_within(2, MAX_SWEEP_POINTS), and mode against a Literal['linear','geometric'] passed explicitly. It then constructs SweepSpec and uses spec.get_values(). One _SWEEP_PARAMETERS table (key, home key, range taken from FLEET_COMPONENTS and the home PV bound) is rendered to the page, and the page renders its options from it. What becomes deletable: the inline validation and math in simulate_sweep, the hard-coded parameterOptions, and _SWEEP_PARAMETER_HOME_KEYS as a separate table. This would have prevented 440, 140 and 128 (unsupported parameters).
findings.verdict_notes: simulate_sweep uses bare float()/int() inside except (ValueError, TypeError), so int(inf) raises an uncaught OverflowError. steps has only a lower bound (steps < 2). Any mode other than 'geometric' runs linear. uuid and math are imported inside the function. parameter-sweep.js ranges are PV 1-20, battery 0-50, consumption 1000-10000, against FLEET_COMPONENTS' wider ranges. A copy of the point generation sits in the JS previewValues (not opened).

findings.title: Preview sampler is a hand copy of config's sampler with a partial copy of its invariants
findings.statement: fleet_config.py::_draw_samples re-implements config's _sample_from_distribution and _DistributionSampler, and re-checks only some of the distribution invariants. It refuses std < 0 and a uniform min > max. It does not refuse a normal with min > max, negative weights, or a values/weights length mismatch. Verified at the pin: sample_distribution('normal', {mean: 4, std: 1, min: 9, max: 2}) returns [2.0, 2.0, 2.0], and weights [-1, 3] draw samples, although NormalDistribution and WeightedDiscreteDistribution.__post_init__ refuse both. Its shuffled pool also cycles past the end of the pool, whereas a run indexes past the end and raises the IndexError that builder_form._scenario_reader_errors catches for 'a shuffled pool smaller than the fleet'. The preview therefore shows histograms for distributions Run refuses, sampled under different rules. The copy exists because config offers no public way to parse one spec and draw from it: _parse_distribution_spec, _sample_from_distribution and _DistributionSampler are all private.
findings.proposal: Expose a narrow public seam in config: parse_distribution_spec(data, path) -> DistributionSpec and draw_values(spec, n, seed) -> list[Optional[float]], the latter wrapping _DistributionSampler so pools behave as a run does. Ideally replace the isinstance chain in _sample_from_distribution with a sample(rng) method on each frozen distribution type (heuristic 3). The preview then becomes editor dist -> grammar spec (the single decoder) -> parse -> draw. That deletes _draw_samples and all its private refusal messages, and the preview refuses exactly what Run refuses. This would have prevented 569, 571 and the per-check patches 520 needed.
findings.verdict_notes: Probed: sample_distribution normal with min=9, max=2 returns [2.0, 2.0, 2.0] where NormalDistribution would refuse it. _draw_samples checks only std<0 and uniform min>max. It has no negative-weight or length checks. Its shuffled pool cycles with i % len(pool). Private config helpers confirmed. My negative-weights probe failed on input shape, but the code has no check.

findings.title: Form bounds and checks restated in page scripts and templates, with no channel from server constants to the fleet and sweep scripts
findings.statement: The maximum fleet size has three values. templates/simulate/fleet.html renders n_homes min 10 and max 500. fleet-simulator.js formErrors refuses n > 1000. The server, through read_fleet_size, allows MAX_FLEET_HOMES = 10_000. formErrors also makes rules of its own that the server does not hold. It refuses std <= 0 and min >= max, where config refuses only std < 0 and min > max. It applies those checks to PV only, not battery or load. fleet-simulator.js holds literal starting distributions that differ from FLEET_COMPONENTS.builder_default: battery max 15.0 against 13.5, load max 6000 against 5000, and a different set of PV rows. This is despite fleet_components' docstring saying both fleet pages render their editors from it. The scripts parseInt n_homes, days and peak hours, so 2.5 is sent as 2, which defeats the server's refuse-fractions policy (498). The PV bound 0.5-20 is a literal in both simulation_params.parse_home_config and home.html (live 612). Server constants reach scripts only through per-page ad-hoc channels: scenarios._script_components for the builder and home.html's consumptionRange. The fleet and sweep scripts receive nothing.
findings.proposal: Add web/form_limits.py::page_limits(), returning one JSON-able frozen value that holds MAX_FLEET_HOMES, MAX_FLEET_SEED, MAX_WINDOW_DAYS, each FleetComponent's fixed_range, step and default editor state, the home PV range (moved into FLEET_COMPONENTS['pv'] or a HOME_PV_RANGE that parse_home_config reads), and the sweep parameters. Inject it through a single Flask context_processor, so every template's min/max and every script reads limits.*. Replace the client-side refusals (formErrors) with the server's answer, as the builder already does through /api/scenarios/validate, and send raw numbers rather than parseInt'd ones. What becomes deletable: fleet.html's 10/500, formErrors, the literal pvDist/batteryDist/loadDist (taken from FLEET_COMPONENTS, with builder_default renamed to default), parameterOptions, home.html's 0.5/20 and the PV literal in parse_home_config. This would have prevented 376, 612, 140, 664, 676 and 522.
findings.verdict_notes: fleet.html has n_homes min=10 max=500. fleet-simulator.js rejects n>1000 and uses parseInt for n_homes, days and peak hours. MAX_FLEET_HOMES = 10_000 in fleet_config.py. JS starting distributions (max 15.0, load max 6000) differ from the FLEET_COMPONENTS builder_default (13.5, 5000). The std<=0 and min>=max rules and the PV-only scope were not individually verified.

findings.title: Two scenario-to-form importers with opposite policies; the builder's runs in the browser and silently drops what it cannot hold
findings.statement: The fleet page imports scenarios on the server. fleet_scenario.fleet_form_from_scenario runs the loaders first, refuses a setting the form needs but cannot hold, and lists the rest in not_loaded. The builder parses the same grammar in the browser with js-yaml, in scenario-builder.js scenarioFormFields and componentDistribution, under the opposite policy: it drops silently. A non-flat_rate tariff becomes import_rate '', so the next preview or save writes tariff: null. A preset SEG becomes ''. dispatch_strategy and every non-capacity component setting vanish with no notice. componentDistribution refuses the 'fixed' type, which fleet_config.distribution_form_spec accepts. js-yaml reads .nan and .inf as numbers (298/549) and unquoted dates as Date objects (554), none of which the loaders see. loadPreset bypasses even scenarioFormFields: it copies name, latitude, longitude and n_homes, with the truthiness reads `cfg.location.latitude || 51.45` and `if (fd.n_homes)`. api.py::scenarios_get_preset returns `config` in two untagged shapes: a scenario document for built-ins, and the flat builder form for saved presets, because scenarios_save_scenario stores getFormData's output without validating it.
findings.proposal: Add builder_form.builder_form_from_scenario(document) -> ImportedForm(form, not_loaded). Build it on fleet_scenario's _read_blocks, _not_loaded and _read_typed_block machinery, moved into a shared web/scenario_import.py so both pages import under one policy. Serve it from /api/scenarios/import-yaml and /api/scenarios/presets/<name>, answering {form, not_loaded} as _loaded_fleet_form_answer does. Saved builder presets would store the scenario document, scenario_from_builder_form's output after builder_form_errors, so built-in and saved presets share one shape. What becomes deletable: scenarioFormFields, componentDistribution, distributionRows, loadPreset's field picking, and the builder page's js-yaml dependency. This would have prevented 298, 545, 549, 553, 554 and 360.
findings.verdict_notes: Core claim holds. scenarioFormFields in scenario-builder.js takes import_rate only when tariff.type === 'flat_rate', else ''. It reads seg only via scenario.seg.rate_pence_per_kwh. loadPreset uses `cfg.location.latitude || 51.45` and `if (fd.n_homes)`. api.py::scenarios_get_preset returns config in two shapes (built-in YAML document vs saved JSON, tagged only by a source field). Overstated: componentDistribution does throw on unsupported shapes (not purely silent), the 'preset SEG becomes empty' case was not shown, and the js-yaml issue numbers were not verified.

findings.title: Docstrings carry the refusal contract transitively and churn with every fix
findings.statement: Docstrings make up 43% of fleet_config.py's raw lines (225 of 545) and 35% of fleet_scenario.py's (188 of 550). Raises sections enumerate refusals transitively: form_to_fleet_distribution_config's points at _component_block, _refuse_battery_dispatch_strategy and _parse_component_distribution, which point further down. fleet_form_from_scenario's docstring is a 20-line policy statement. That prose is the contract a typed refusal or a single grammar owner would carry. Of the window's 94 non-merge commits on the five Python core files, 26 are amend: commits, several docstring-only, whose job was keeping this prose in step with the code: 1ea7939, 6830f03, b62bba5, 1c0fbb2, 6d2ca16 and a90340c. 6d2ca16 described a truncating integer reader that 650 later removed.
findings.proposal: Once the number invariant and the grammar sit in config and a single decoder, as the first two findings propose, each Raises section shrinks to 'ConfigurationError from config's fleet_distribution grammar; ValueError from read_editor_distribution'. Policy prose such as fleet_form_from_scenario's (what the form holds, what it refuses, what goes in not_loaded) moves to a tracked docs/web-fleet-forms.md, with a one-line pointer from the code.

findings.verdict_notes: Docstring line counts confirmed by ast: 225 of 545 in fleet_config.py and 188 of 550 in fleet_scenario.py (about 41% and 34%). Transitive Raises sections are visible (form_to_fleet_distribution_config). Low severity as stated; the amend-commit counts and named SHAs were not verified.

findings.title: No field-level typed reader: each config.py block reader decides coercion, bool, NaN and truncation on its own
findings.statement: config.py has 51 numeric coercion sites, and no one reader enforces the rule 'a finite number, never a bool, a whole number where a count is meant, refused with the key path'. The block readers use three different styles. (a) Raw splat into the domain dataclass: _parse_pv_config, _parse_battery_config, _parse_load_config, _parse_grid_charge_config, and parse_home_block's scalar keys. The component __post_init__ checks bounds only, never type. (b) Inline float(), int() or str(): _parse_heat_pump_config, _parse_ev_config, _build_shuffled_pool_spec, _parse_proportional_to_multiplier, parse_fleet_distribution_config's int(data['n_homes']), _parse_event_windows, and _parse_distribution_spec's isinstance(data, (int, float)), which lets True through. (c) Tables over _number or _number_or_none: the finance and grid-services blocks only. whole_numbers.whole_number is used nowhere in config.py. Probes at 7dfea36 confirm each style's failure. `pv: {capacity_kw: true}` builds a PVConfig whose capacity_kw is the bool True. `azimuth: south` raises a raw TypeError from PVConfig.__post_init__, and cli/utils.handle_errors does not catch TypeError. `use_stochastic: 'no'` is kept as a truthy string. `heat_pump: {thermal_capacity_kw: .nan}` is accepted, because HeatPumpConfig's `<= 0` and `> 50` comparisons are both False for NaN. Location altitude NaN is accepted the same way. `arrival_hour: 18.9` becomes 18, `n_homes: 2.7` becomes 2, `n_homes: true` becomes 1, and a distribution capacity_kw of true becomes 1.0. A null annual_heat_demand_kwh raises a raw TypeError from float(None). The project already has the right reader, in the web layer: web/number_fields.as_finite_float, as_whole_number and their *_within variants. Because config.py lacks it, the web layer compensates. web/fleet_scenario._read_fleet_size_and_seed reads n_homes and seed itself, 'ahead of the loaders, whose int() would refuse n_homes first, naming no setting'.
findings.proposal: Add a module below config.py, scenario_fields.py, beside whole_numbers.py. It holds typed field readers that all raise ConfigurationError naming the full key path and the value given: finite_number(value, path, low=None, high=None), whole_number_field(value, path, low, high), boolean_field(value, path) (only a YAML bool) and choice(value, path, allowed). Move the rule now in web/number_fields into it, and turn number_fields into a thin ValueError adapter over it. Express every block reader as a declarative key-to-reader table, the shape _FINANCE_SCALAR_COERCIONS already has, applied by one function, read_block(block_path, data, table, cls). That function refuses unrecognised keys, reads each present key through its reader, and constructs cls with only those keys, so omitted keys take the dataclass default. This deletes _number, _number_or_none and _float_or_none, the finite check in _parse_seg_rate_scalar, the inline float(), int() and str() calls, and the web pre-read in _read_fleet_size_and_seed. It would have prevented tasks 374, 384 and 498 and the live tasks 314, 382, 521, 558, 559, 570, 573, 616, 618, 651, 675 and 678: each becomes one table row, not a separate fix.

findings.verdict_notes: Probes at the pin: pv capacity_kw true builds a PVConfig holding True; azimuth 'south' raises a raw TypeError; heat_pump_type is also case-strict. _number and _number_or_none are the only shared readers. whole_number is not referenced in config.py.

findings.title: Every component's fields and defaults are restated through the distribution, sampler and sweep layers
findings.statement: PVConfig's defaults (azimuth 180.0, tilt 35.0, module_efficiency 0.20, inverter_efficiency 0.96, degradation_rate_per_year 0.005) are written four times: in pv.py::PVConfig, in config.py::PVDistributionConfig's field defaults, in config.py::_parse_pv_distribution_config's data.get(..., 180.0) calls, and in config.py::generate_homes_from_distribution's `pv_azimuth if pv_azimuth is not None else 180.0` fallbacks. EV defaults (departure 7, required 35.0, mode 'none') appear in ev.py::EVConfig, _parse_ev_config, EVDistributionConfig, _parse_ev_distribution_config and generate_homes_from_distribution. Heat-pump 8.0 and 8000.0 appear in four places, and battery 2.5 kW in four. Each layer also restates which fields it carries, and they already disagree. The distribution grammar has no temperature_coefficient, inverter_capacity_kw or system_losses for PV, and no SOC limits, efficiencies or degradation for batteries. The sweep rebuilders copy fields by hand: _modify_pv_config drops system_losses and the custom pvlib params, and _modify_battery_config drops dispatch_strategy, grid_charging, the SOC limits, the efficiencies and the degradation fields. A probe confirms a battery-capacity sweep resets grid_charging to None and min_soc to 0.1. generate_homes_from_distribution reaches cognitive complexity 45 largely through these per-component None-fallback branches. The PRDs for financial-layer battery fidelity and live-sim PV degradation already require threading each new field through every one of these sites by hand.
findings.proposal: Make the domain dataclass the only statement of a component's fields and defaults. The sampler builds each component as Cls(**{k: v for k, v in sampled.items() if v is not None}), so an unsampled or null field takes the dataclass default, and the `else 180.0` fallbacks and the *DistributionConfig default values are deleted. Derive each *DistributionConfig's recognised keys from dataclasses.fields(Cls), minus an explicit per-component set of fields the distribution grammar does not sample, and parse each value through _parse_distribution_spec. Replace _modify_pv_config, _modify_battery_config and _modify_load_config with dataclasses.replace. That deletes about 150 lines of copy-constructors and the restated defaults in four places per component. It removes the 'thread through every construction site' cost from future field additions, and it would have prevented f5c5356 and the live tasks 599, 600, 237 and 320.
findings.bug_history_link: f5c5356 fix(config): preserve system_age_years + degradation_rate_per_year in _modify_pv_config; 7be9cfc fix(381) sweep and fleet distribution battery presence; 25860e1 and be3ca77 (FLEET_COMPONENTS bounds, tasks 566 and 613); live tasks 599, 600, 237, 320
findings.verdict_notes: _modify_battery_config rebuilds BatteryConfig from only capacity, charge kW, discharge kW and name, so it drops grid_charging, SOC limits, efficiencies and the other fields. The PV default 180.0 is repeated across pv.py and config.py (three hits in config.py, not a verified four). Overall the duplication is real.

findings.title: Document shape is classified by checking top-level keys in five or more places, and `home run` edits the raw dict before parsing
findings.statement: Which document a config file is (a scenario list, one scenario, a bare scenario, a wrapped or flat home file, fleet homes, a fleet distribution, a YAML sweep) is decided by testing for top-level keys. Each of these makes that decision on its own, with its own order and fallback: config.py::load_scenarios ('scenarios', then 'scenario', else the whole document), config.py::load_home_config ('home', else a flat file), config.py::parse_fleet_config ('fleet_distribution', then 'homes'), cli/validate.py::_homes_defined_by (its own precedence), cli/fleet.py::sweep, web/fleet_scenario.py::_fleet_scenario, and cli/home.py::home_config_for_run. The last of these goes through cli/utils.load_config_with_overrides, which mutates the raw loaded dict and inserts an empty `home: {pv: {}, load: {}}` before any parsing. As a result, a flat home file that load_home_config and `validate config` read as 9 kW runs under `home run` as the default 4 kW home (probed at 7dfea36). Apart from load_home_config's flat form, no shape refuses unrecognised top-level keys. The CLI's location override also writes a location block by hand, restating scenario_writer.location_block.
findings.proposal: Add one classifier in config.py, read_config_document(document) -> ConfigDocument. ConfigDocument is a tagged union of frozen types (HomeDocument, ScenarioDocument, FleetHomesDocument, FleetDistributionDocument), and each type refuses top-level keys its shape does not read. Every CLI and web entry point dispatches on the returned type rather than on key presence. Apply CLI overrides to the parsed HomeConfig with dataclasses.replace after parsing; a --battery-kwh replaces only capacity_kwh. That deletes load_config_with_overrides' dict surgery, _homes_defined_by's key tests, _FLAT_HOME_FILE_KEYS, the shape checks in cli/fleet.sweep and the duplicate location-block literal. It would have prevented the fixes for tasks 14, 315, 340 and 396, and the live tasks 422, 485, 186, 325, 542, 681 and 528.

findings.verdict_notes: load_config_with_overrides mutates the raw dict and inserts home/pv/load when 'home' is absent, so a flat home file loses its keys under home run. Top-level shape detection is spread across the loaders and CLI sites as claimed.

findings.title: scenario_writer.py and config.py's readers are two grammars kept in step by hand, and the writer already drops PVConfig.system_losses
findings.statement: They are two grammars kept in step by hand, not one. Each writer block in scenario_writer.py (_pv_block, _battery_block, _load_block, _heat_pump_block, _ev_block, location_block) lists the component's keys again as a dict literal. Those lists repeat config.py's _PV_BLOCK_KEYS, _BATTERY_BLOCK_KEYS and the rest, which in turn repeat the dataclass fields. All that holds them together is a CLAUDE.md sentence ('change both together') and tests/unit/test_scenario_writer.py, whose `_every_grammar_field_home` fixture names fields by hand. A field missing from both the reader and the writer therefore passes the round-trip test. This has already happened: pv.py::PVConfig.system_losses is in neither _PV_BLOCK_KEYS nor _pv_block. _pv_block's guard against fields it cannot express names only custom_module_params and custom_inverter_params. So a HomeConfig with system_losses=0.05 is written without complaint and reads back as 0.1408 (probed at 7dfea36). The writer's docstring also says null is read back 'as their default or None', but _parse_heat_pump_config raises a raw TypeError on a null annual_heat_demand_kwh.
findings.proposal: Derive both directions from one table per component, a field-to-reader table (the read_block table of the field-reader finding) keyed by dataclass field. The writer emits {f: getattr(cfg, f) for f in table}. The writer refuses a config that sets a field outside the table to a non-default value, so the set of inexpressible fields is computed from dataclasses.fields(Cls) minus the table, not a hand-kept deny-list. Add one parametrised test: for each component, dataclasses.fields(Cls) == table keys plus a declared, reviewed set of non-grammar fields. Adding a field then fails a test until someone decides about it. That deletes the per-block dict literals in scenario_writer.py and the CLAUDE.md 'change both together' rule.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative for the history; the system_losses drop is a present-tree defect not filed in the live context given. Related: PRD financial-layer-battery-fidelity (battery.efficiency parsed then dropped)
findings.verdict_notes: system_losses appears in neither _PV_BLOCK_KEYS in config.py nor scenario_writer.py, though PVConfig has the field, so the writer drops it silently.

findings.title: Block readers hand raw values to domain constructors, so refusals carry no block path and some escape as TypeError
findings.statement: Every reader receives block_path, but only _refuse_unrecognised_keys, _require_mapping and a few messages use it. Errors raised inside the domain constructors pass through unchanged. For example `ValueError: Azimuth must be 0-360 degrees, got 400` names neither `homes[37].pv.azimuth` nor the file's block. Messages such as "Dispatch strategy config requires 'strategy_type'", "Tariff period requires 'start_time' field", "heat_pump configuration requires 'heat_pump_type' field" and "PV distribution config requires 'capacity_kw'" leave out the path the reader holds. Error types are also split. PVConfig, BatteryConfig, LoadConfig, HeatPumpConfig, EVConfig and Location raise ValueError. GridChargeConfig, DispatchStrategyConfig, FinanceConfig and FleetDistributionConfig raise ConfigurationError. Wrongly typed values raise TypeError, which cli/utils.handle_errors does not catch, so the user gets a traceback. _parse_event_windows and parse_finance_config each wrap the error with their own phrase ('contains a non-numeric value'), which shows the missing shared mechanism being patched block by block.
findings.proposal: Give read_block (see the field-reader finding) one construction boundary: build(block_path, Cls, fields). It calls Cls(**fields) and re-raises any ValueError, TypeError or ConfigurationError as ConfigurationError(f'{block_path}: {exc}'), chaining the cause. Every reader constructs through it, and each 'requires X' check becomes a required-key entry in the reader's table, worded uniformly with the path. That deletes the wrapping try/except blocks in _parse_event_windows, _parse_grid_services_events_config and parse_finance_config, and handle_errors no longer has to guess at domain exception types. It would have prevented the fix for task 4e3ae52/374 ('parse_finance_config raises only ConfigurationError') and the live tasks 328, 377, 563, 423 and 603.
findings.bug_history_link: 4e3ae52 fix(374) parse_finance_config raises only ConfigurationError; live tasks 328, 377, 563, 423 (raw TypeError and AttributeError), 603
findings.verdict_notes: cli/utils.py::handle_errors catches ConfigurationError, FileNotFoundError, ValueError and WeatherDataError, not TypeError. The probe with a string azimuth escaped as TypeError. Domain-constructor errors do not carry the block path.

findings.title: ConfigurationError, GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig sit at the top of the stack, so lower modules reach back with deferred imports
findings.statement: config.py imports battery, finance, gridservices, fleet and home at module level. Yet the error type and two battery-domain value types those modules need are defined in config.py. gridservices.py contains 9 function-local `from solar_challenge.config import ConfigurationError` lines, and its module docstring carries an 'Import cycle note' defending them. finance.py has 2 more, one commented 'lazy: avoids import cycle'. battery.py imports GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig from config.py under TYPE_CHECKING, because BatteryConfig's fields are typed with classes defined in the module above it. Those are heuristic-13 symptoms: function-local imports placed to break a cycle, and a reach-back from a lower module into its parent. The same placement means the battery-domain rules in GridChargeConfig.__post_init__ and DispatchStrategyConfig.__post_init__ are enforced in the grammar module rather than next to Battery. tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py pins them in FROZEN_CLOSURE as 'config.GridChargeConfig' and 'config.DispatchStrategyConfig'.
findings.proposal: Move ConfigurationError to a leaf module, solar_challenge/errors.py, and make it subclass ValueError so existing `except ValueError` handlers keep working. config.py imports it for its own use. That use is real, so the import is not a re-export shim. Move GridChargeConfig to battery.py and DispatchStrategyConfig to dispatch.py. Both are in the frozen closure under config.*, so this needs the deliberate version bump the briefing's frozen-API convention requires, plus updates to the FROZEN_CLOSURE rows. If that bump is refused, move only ConfigurationError. That deletes the 11 function-local imports, gridservices.py's import-cycle docstring paragraph and battery.py's TYPE_CHECKING block. It is also a precondition for the config.py split measured in the god-module finding.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (no fix commit traced to the cycle itself); it is the structure behind the 13 deferred imports flagged by the metrics snapshot
findings.verdict_notes: ConfigurationError, GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig are defined in config.py (lines 35, 254, 356). gridservices.py has 9 function-local `from solar_challenge.config import` lines and finance.py has 3 (one of them may be module-level or TYPE_CHECKING). battery.py imports from config only under TYPE_CHECKING.

also_reported_as.title: ConfigurationError lives in config.py, which imports finance and gridservices, so they break the cycle with 11 function-local imports and paragraphs defending them
also_reported_as.statement: config.py imports `from solar_challenge.finance import FinanceConfig` and `from solar_challenge.gridservices import EventWindow, GridServicesEventsConfig` at module level, while defining ConfigurationError itself. Both lower modules therefore raise it through function-local imports placed to break the cycle. These are finance.py::FinanceConfig.__post_init__ (commented 'lazy: avoids import cycle'), finance.py::project_multi_year, gridservices.py::GridServicesEventsConfig.__post_init__, and eight separate `from solar_challenge.config import ConfigurationError` lines, one per failing branch, in gridservices.py::EventWindow.__post_init__. That last method carries a 15-line docstring and further module-docstring prose explaining why a top-level import would fire during module initialisation. The prose is reviewer-answering rationale, which the Comments stance says belongs in a commit, and every new validator in these files has to repeat the ritual. finance.py also holds eight more function-local imports (fleet.simulate_fleet and FleetConfig twice, home.calculate_summary twice, pv.calculate_degradation_factor, battery.compute_soh, gridservices.compute_grid_services_at_events) that close no cycle at all. None of fleet, home, pv, battery or gridservices imports finance or config, so a reader has to work out which local imports are load-bearing.

findings.title: run_parameter_sweep and its copy-constructors have no production caller, yet live tasks are still repairing them
findings.statement: At 7dfea36 the only callers of run_parameter_sweep, ParameterSweepConfig and SweepResult are in tests/unit/config/test_parameter_sweep.py, and none of them is in solar_challenge.__all__. The real sweep paths are cli/fleet.py::sweep, which uses substitute_config_variables and parse_sweep_fleet_configs, and the SweepSpec multiplier. So there are two sweep mechanisms. The unused one routes on string parameter names held in hard-coded sets ('pv_capacity_kw', 'battery_charge_kw' and others), and rebuilds HomeConfig without heat_pump_config, ev_config or seg_tariff. It rebuilds components field by field and drops fields: a probe shows a battery-capacity sweep losing grid_charging and min_soc_fraction. It truncates household_occupants with int(value). It is also the only reason config.py imports simulate_home and simulate_fleet, which ties the grammar module to the simulation runners.
findings.proposal: Delete run_parameter_sweep, _apply_parameter_to_home, the three _modify_* functions, ParameterSweepConfig and SweepResult, along with their test file. If a scenario-level sweep is wanted later, express it with the fleet path's SweepSpec and dataclasses.replace. That removes about 210 lines and config.py's dependence on the runners. Close live tasks 237 and 320 as obsolete rather than fixing dead code. It retroactively explains f5c5356.

findings.title: config.py is a god module (grammar, fleet sampler, loaders, substitution, sweep runner); the heuristic-14 measurement says what must move first
findings.statement: Stating config.py's purpose takes 'and': it reads scenario files, samples fleets, substitutes variables, expands sweeps and runs simulations. Measurement at 7dfea36: 2815 lines, of which 511 are blank, 665 docstring and 60 comment, so prose is 21.2%. Prose is not what makes the file large; about 1,580 lines are code. The top-level symbols split into named candidates. (1) The fleet-distribution grammar and sampler: the distribution types, the *DistributionConfig classes, the distribution parsers, _DistributionSampler, generate_homes_from_distribution, detect_sweep_spec and expand_sweep_configs, about 1,100 lines. (2) The finance, SEG and grid-services block readers, about 190 lines. (3) The community readers, about 140 lines. (4) The parameter-sweep runner, about 210 lines. (5) Variable substitution, about 55 lines, with a mid-file `import re`. (6) The core: the primitives, the home blocks, _parse_scenario and the loaders. Heuristic-13 symptom for each. Candidates 1, 2 and 3 would stitch today. fleet_distribution.py would need `from solar_challenge.config import ConfigurationError, _refuse_unrecognised_keys, _child_path, _BlockType, _parse_grid_charge_config, parse_dispatch_strategy_config, GridChargeConfig, DispatchStrategyConfig`, while config.py::parse_fleet_config and _read_fleet_distribution_file import parse_fleet_distribution_config and generate_homes_from_distribution from it: a config.py <-> fleet_distribution.py cycle through private names. The finance and community readers would reach back the same way for the primitives, while _parse_scenario and load_community_config import them. Candidate 4 shows no symptom: config.py never calls it, it would import ScenarioConfig downward, and it has no production caller (see the redundant-abstraction finding). Candidate 5 shows no symptom; it needs only ConfigurationError. Task 177 (this measurement) is still pending.
findings.proposal: Split in an order that never stitches. First, move the block primitives (_child_path, _require_mapping, _refuse_unrecognised_keys, _BlockType) and the scenario_fields readers into a lower module, scenario_blocks.py, which imports only errors.py and whole_numbers.py. Move ConfigurationError, GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig down as the porous-boundary finding proposes. Move the home-block readers that the distribution grammar reuses (parse_dispatch_strategy_config, _parse_grid_charge_config) into it as well, under public names. Then extract fleet_distribution.py, finance_blocks.py and community_blocks.py, each importing only scenario_blocks.py and domain modules, with config.py importing them downward. Delete the sweep runner rather than moving it. Move substitution into a variables.py leaf. Record this measurement in the split task's commit message, not in the module docstring.

findings.verdict_notes: The file is 2815 lines. It holds the grammar, the sampler, the loaders, the sweep runner (line 2465 on) and a mid-file `import re` at line 2072. The cycle claims for the proposed split are plausible but only asserted; I did not trace each one.

findings.title: Pricing provenance is lost at simulate_home; finance re-infers 'is this priced?' and unit rates from money totals, three times, with three different fallbacks
findings.statement: home.py::simulate_home encodes 'no tariff' as a priced cost of 0.0 for every timestep (`import_costs = [0.0 ...]` when tariff_config is None) and 'no SEG' as export revenue of 0.0. home.py::SummaryStatistics then carries only the totals total_import_cost_gbp and total_export_revenue_gbp. It does not carry whether they were priced, or at what rate. Finance has to rebuild that lost fact from the totals. (1) finance.py::_physics_import_cost_gbp decides 'unpriced' as `import_cost_physics == 0.0 and import_kwh > 0.0` and re-prices at retail. A tariff that really costs £0 (live task 690), or a TOU tariff whose window import all falls in a 0p period, is therefore billed at retail with a false 'no tariff configured' warning. (2) finance.py::householder_bill's override branch gets an import unit rate as `import_cost_physics / import_kwh`, falling back to retail when physics import is 0. (3) finance.py::_seg_export_income_gbp gets a SEG rate as `export_rev_physics / export_kwh`, falling back to 0.0 when physics export is 0. A home whose battery absorbed all physics export, but whose override implies (1 - override) x generation of export, therefore earns the CBS £0 SEG, even though HomeConfig.seg_tariff holds a real rate. TestSegExportIncome's 'zero physics export returns 0.0' test in tests/unit/test_finance_projection_revenue.py pins that loss as the contract, and it reaches the private _seg_export_income_gbp and _annualise_physics to do it. Every fix in this class patched the inference rather than the lost fact. 8dffcf8 added the retail fallback. 613e306 (307) moved it before the override switch. 690 is live for the £0 tariff. a17acbc/a0e572d (85) removed an import-rate export fallback. Units diverge as well: tariff.TariffPeriod.rate_per_kwh is in £/kWh, SEGTariff in p/kWh and FinanceConfig in p/kWh (live 229: pence-to-GBP written twice).
findings.proposal: Carry pricing as data across the physics->finance boundary instead of inferring it from totals. Add to SummaryStatistics (an additive change, as the frozen-contract procedure allows) a typed `pricing: FlowPricing` record. It holds `import_priced: bool` (tariff present), `import_rate_mean_gbp_per_kwh` (the flow-weighted import rate) and `seg_rate_pence_per_kwh: Optional[float]` taken from HomeConfig.seg_tariff. simulate_home and calculate_summary are its only writer. Finance reads it in one function, `price_billed_flows(ledger_kwh, pricing, finance)`. That function prices import at the home's own rate (retail only when import_priced is False) and override export at the home's SEG rate. It warns only on the explicit unpriced flag. What becomes deletable: the `== 0.0 and > 0.0` sentinel test in _physics_import_cost_gbp, householder_bill's effective_import_rate_pence derivation, _seg_export_income_gbp's effective_export_rate_pence derivation and its 0.0 fallback, and the test that pins £0 SEG. This would have prevented 8dffcf8, 307, 690 and the zero-physics-export SEG loss, and it gives 229's unit conversion one home.
findings.bug_history_link: 8dffcf8 fix(finance): price physics imports at retail baseline when tariff absent; 613e306 fix(307); a17acbc/a0e572d (task 85 import-rate export fallback); live 690 (GBP0/kWh tariff billed at retail), 229 (pence-to-GBP twice); the zero-physics-export SEG loss is not in the live task context (new)
findings.verdict_notes: finance.py::_physics_import_cost_gbp tests `import_cost_physics == 0.0 and import_kwh > 0.0` and reprices at retail with a 'no tariff configured' warning. home.py::simulate_home sets import_costs to zeros when tariff_config is None, and SummaryStatistics carries only totals. finance.py::householder_bill derives the import rate as cost/kWh, falling back to retail. finance.py::_seg_export_income_gbp falls back to 0.0 when physics export is 0, ignoring HomeConfig.seg_tariff. All three inference sites exist as described.

findings.title: Householder bill and CBS revenue are two hand-assembled ledgers over one per-home money flow, with no shared record and no double-entry invariant
findings.statement: One home's annual flows (own-use, import and its cost, export and its SEG) are put together twice. householder_bill annualises, applies the retail fallback, switches physics/override through _billed_energy, re-prices import and calls bill. project_multi_year._simulate_age annualises again, calls _billed_energy with `_cbs_own_use_kwh(s) * phys.scale`, sums physics export and import, and calls _seg_export_income_gbp, which recomputes _override_energy_split on its own. The two sides share helpers one at a time, and no invariant ties them together: for each home, nothing checks that the own-use kWh the householder pays for is the own-use kWh the CBS earns on, that own_use + import == demand, or that own_use + export == generation. Every basis bug in the history was a disagreement between these two assemblies. 219 had grid-charge cost on both ledgers. 271 had window own-use on the CBS side against annual everything else. 281/308 had override own-use capped on the bill but not driving CBS revenue. 307 had the override path pricing import differently. They still disagree today. Under the override, YearPoint.fleet_export_kwh and fleet_import_kwh are the physics flows, while the SEG part of fleet_revenue_gbp is priced on override export. That contradicts YearPoint's own docstring claim that '£/kWh derivations from a YearPoint are consistent'. Names compound it (heuristic 1). YearPoint.fleet_self_consumption_kwh holds billed own-use; its docstring spends 20 lines saying not to read it as self-consumption, and it is the rate base of solve_cost_recovery_rate.surplus_at. BillDistribution.per_home_net_bill_gbp holds total outlay (a briefing known gap). Tests reach the private helpers directly (test_finance_projection_revenue.py imports _seg_export_income_gbp and _annualise_physics; test_finance_bill.py imports _cbs_own_use_kwh), which shows the ledger is a real seam with no public interface.
findings.proposal: Introduce one frozen per-home value `HomeLedger` (generation_kwh, demand_kwh, own_use_kwh, import_kwh, import_cost_gbp, export_kwh, seg_income_gbp, own_use_capped: bool), produced by a single `annual_ledger(summary, finance) -> HomeLedger` that does the annualisation, the physics/override split and the pricing (through the FlowPricing record of the previous finding). Its __post_init__ enforces the balances (own_use + import == demand; on the override path own_use + export == generation), non-negativity and finiteness. householder_bill becomes `bill(**ledger fields)` plus warnings. _simulate_age sums ledgers: fleet own-use, fleet export and fleet import all come from the ledgers, so revenue and energy share one basis. Make it a public module seam (a `billing`/`ledger` module) and point the tests at it. Add `fleet_billed_own_use_kwh` and `per_home_total_outlay_gbp`, keeping the old names as frozen-contract deprecated aliases. What becomes deletable: _billed_energy, _override_energy_split's second caller in _seg_export_income_gbp, householder_bill's override branch, the per-home `_cbs_own_use_kwh(s) * phys.scale` re-annualisation in _simulate_age, and the 20-line 'do not treat this field as' note on YearPoint. This would have prevented the 219, 271, 281, 307 and 308 class.
findings.bug_history_link: 93f9fde fix(219); 29bd585/515446d fix(271); 2cc7908/0dbb044 fix(281); 129ab48 fix(308); 613e306 fix(307); briefing known gap per_home_net_bill_gbp
findings.verdict_notes: householder_bill and project_multi_year._simulate_age both annualise physics and call _billed_energy. _simulate_age also calls _seg_export_income_gbp, which recomputes _override_energy_split. No shared record ties the two ledgers. The helper-only seam is visible in the code. I did not individually verify each historical basis bug or the YearPoint docstring wording.

findings.title: Scenario-level pricing overlays (seg, tariff_config) have no single resolver: stored as raw scalars on ScenarioConfig and threaded, or dropped, by each consumer
findings.statement: Two fields on config.py::ScenarioConfig hold unresolved pricing overlays: seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh and tariff_config. Neither is applied to HomeConfig at parse time. The SEG rate is applied separately in each of these places: cli/finance.py::run (parse_seg_rate, then `SEGTariff(name="", ...)` and replace on every home), cli/optimize.py::configs (the same block written again), cli/home.py::home_config_for_run (a third copy), finance.py::_reconcile_seg_homes (its docstring says it 'mirrors the threading workaround in cli/finance.py:162-169'; it is called from both project_multi_year and solve_cost_recovery_rate), and optimize.py::_repriced_at_seg_rate (286 had to write homes and scenario together). optimize.py::_age0_baseline_outlay reconciles nothing at all, and commit 826ffd3 says the knob writes homes 'because _age0_baseline_outlay simulates the scenario's homes without any reconciliation'. Meanwhile finance and optimize pass scenario.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh into calculate_summary at three sites (finance.py _simulate_age, finance.py solve_cost_recovery_rate, optimize.py _age0_baseline_outlay). That only fills SummaryStatistics.seg_revenue_gbp, which no finance code reads. cli/finance.py::run therefore threads the scenario rate only under --cost-recovery, and its comment claims this 'avoids silently changing project_multi_year SEG revenue'. The branch is inert, because the homes already carry the tariff, so the comment is false. ScenarioConfig.tariff_config has no reader anywhere in src/. A scenario-level tariff is parsed and dropped, which leaves homes untariffed and sends them into finance's retail fallback. The live tasks are the same defect seen from different consumers: 185 (fleet run ignores top-level seg), 187 (community seg_rate scalar), 296 (one helper to set SEG on scenario and homes), 287, 186 and 541 (scenario loading duplicated).
findings.proposal: Resolve overlays once, at the parse boundary. A single `resolve_scenario_pricing(raw_document) -> list[HomeConfig]` (or HomeConfig.with_pricing_overlay, the seam task 186 proposes), owned by config.py's scenario grammar, applies `seg:` and `tariff_config:` to every home and refuses a conflicting per-home rate there, with the message _reconcile_seg_homes uses today. Both CLIs, the web overlay and _parse_scenario call it. Under the frozen-contract procedure, ScenarioConfig.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh and tariff_config become derived or deprecated, and finance reads only HomeConfig.seg_tariff and tariff_config. What becomes deletable: _reconcile_seg_homes and its two call sites, the three CLI threading blocks, the scenario-field half of _repriced_at_seg_rate, the three `calculate_summary(..., seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh=scenario...)` arguments in finance and optimize, cli/finance's --cost-recovery-only threading branch and its comment, and the 'reconcile or not' reasoning in 826ffd3. This would have prevented 89, 185, 286 and the dropped scenario tariff_config.

findings.verdict_notes: SEGTariff(name='', ...) is built in cli/finance.py::run, cli/optimize.py (line ~227), cli/home.py (line ~56) and optimize.py::_repriced_at_seg_rate. finance._reconcile_seg_homes is called from both project_multi_year and solve_cost_recovery_rate. optimize._age0_baseline_outlay calls only _resolve_homes and does no reconciliation. cli/finance.py threads the scenario rate only under cost_recovery, and the homes already carry the tariff, so that branch is inert and its comment misleading. A grep found no reader of ScenarioConfig.tariff_config in src. Only home.tariff_config is read.

findings.title: ScenarioConfig is the wrong input for projection/solve: each entry re-resolves the fleet and re-runs an age-0 simulation, and the copies have diverged
findings.statement: project_multi_year, solve_cost_recovery_rate and optimize._age0_baseline_outlay each take a ScenarioConfig. That is a home-or-homes union with a FinanceConfig field the callees ignore in favour of a separately passed `finance`. Each callee redoes the same resolution (_resolve_homes, the scenario.location-or-first-home timezone, period.get_start/end_timestamp), and optimize imports finance's private _resolve_homes to do it. The age-0 per-home simulation is written three times, and the copies disagree. solve_cost_recovery_rate step 6 uses `_aged_homes(homes, 0)`, which overwrites every battery's soh with compute_soh(0, 0), i.e. a new battery, after _reconcile_seg_homes. optimize._age0_baseline_outlay ages only PV to 0, leaves a configured battery soh or system_age_years in place, and skips SEG reconciliation. A scenario with an aged battery therefore ranks ConfigResult.baseline_outlay_gbp and representative_outlay_gbp on different fleets. The solve hides the intermediate results callers need. It already computes base_curve at finance.own_use_rate, yet _evaluate_config calls project_multi_year again with identical arguments (3-12 fleet simulations re-run per config) and then runs a fourth age-0 simulation for a bill that is affine in the rate. cli/optimize.py's large-sweep comment ('up to 3 fleet simulations') understates the real count of up to 2 x MAX_NODES + 2. Other agents' known context: 582 (age-0 outlay sim written twice) and 515 (FleetSimulator callable type restated 7 times).
findings.proposal: Introduce a frozen `ResolvedFleetRun` (homes: tuple[HomeConfig, ...] with pricing already resolved, start_ts, end_ts, simulate), built by one `resolve_fleet_run(scenario, simulate)`. Make it the only input of project_multi_year, solve_cost_recovery_rate and project_economics, keeping ScenarioConfig-accepting wrappers for the frozen API. project_multi_year returns the age-0 per-home SummaryStatistics alongside the curve (or a `ProjectionRun` record). CostRecoverySolution exposes base_curve and the age-0 summaries, so _evaluate_config gets baseline surplus as project_economics(base_curve) and baseline outlay as bill_distribution(age0_summaries, finance) with no new simulation. Name one `FleetSimulator` Protocol (task 515). What becomes deletable: three timezone/period derivations, optimize's import of finance._resolve_homes, _age0_baseline_outlay entirely, solve step 6's re-simulation, and the duplicate project_multi_year in _evaluate_config. The diverging-battery bug cannot happen, because one age-0 node feeds every consumer.

findings.title: Grid-services model is a string selector over two optional fields; the 'events required' invariant is checked at four points that disagree, not at construction
findings.statement: FinanceConfig encodes one variability axis, how grid-services income is priced, as three fields: `grid_services_model: str` (checked against a local _VALID_GS_MODELS frozenset), `grid_services_income_per_kw_per_year_gbp` (meaningful only for 'flat') and `grid_services_events: Optional[...]` (meaningful only for 'capacity_at_events'). FinanceConfig accepts capacity_at_events with events None; its docstring says 'α only validates the selector field'. The other points handle that pair differently. project_multi_year raises ConfigurationError, via a function-local import, before simulating. _simulate_age repeats the string compare and asserts. cli/finance.py::run quietly renders no events section (`... and finance.grid_services_events is not None else None`). cli/optimize.py::configs writes --grid-services-kw into the flat field, which is ignored without warning under the events model. The mode is branched on inline in _simulate_age and cli/finance.run. Each pricing method lives in a different place: the flat sum is inline in _simulate_age, and the events income comes from gridservices.compute_grid_services_at_events through a closure memo dict, `_event_gs_memo["value"]`, which is the briefing's known age-0 memo gap. The band vocabulary 'low/central/high' is another stringly-typed axis, restated in flex.FLEX_VALUE_BANDS keys, gridservices.GridServicesRateBands.resolve's if-chain, GridServicesEventsConfig's _VALID_BANDS, and cli/finance.FlexBand.
findings.proposal: Make the axis one typed mechanism. Use `GridServicesModel = FlatGridServices(income_per_kw_per_year_gbp) | CapacityAtEventsGridServices(events: GridServicesEventsConfig)`, each a frozen dataclass with `annual_income_gbp(homes, age0_fleet_results) -> float`, and give FinanceConfig a single `grid_services: GridServicesModel` field. config.py's parse_finance_config maps the YAML onto it. The legacy three fields remain as frozen-contract deprecated constructor arguments that build the union in __post_init__ and refuse an inconsistent combination there. Under that design capacity_at_events without events cannot be constructed. Give the band vocabulary one `Band` enum in gridservices. What becomes deletable: _VALID_GS_MODELS, project_multi_year's fail-fast guard and its lazy import, _simulate_age's if/else and assert, cli/finance's conjunction, and the silent no-op of --grid-services-kw (optimize then refuses it under the events model). The memo becomes an explicit age-0 input rather than closure state, which makes the known SOH-tracking gap a visible parameter.

findings.title: Finiteness is enforced in parsers and at the projection's tail, not in the input value types: SEGTariff, EventWindow, GridServicesEventsConfig and FlexibilityValueBand still admit NaN/inf
findings.statement: No shared 'finite and in range' rule exists, so each frozen type writes its own comparison and the guards differ. FinanceConfig uses `0.0 <= v < math.inf` (fixed by 374). SEGTariff.__post_init__ uses `rate < 0`, which admits NaN and +inf. config.py::_parse_seg_rate_scalar compensates by checking math.isfinite before it builds SEGTariff, but that guards only YAML input. The optimize 'seg' knob (optimize._repriced_at_seg_rate), community's seg_rate scalar (live 187) and any library caller construct SEGTariff directly. gridservices.py::EventWindow uses `events_per_year <= 0` and `event_hours <= 0.0`, and GridServicesEventsConfig's two overrides use `< 0`, all of which admit NaN and inf. flex.py::FlexibilityValueBand uses `< 0` on four fields. A non-finite value from any of these flows into fleet_revenue and is first refused by _NodeData.__post_init__ (656), which runs only after a full age-0 fleet simulation, or by YearPoint (652). Those checks are guards at the end of the pipeline, standing in for invariants on the inputs. The history shows the pattern: 374, 381, 652 x5 and 656 each closed one type, and live 382, 659, 660 and 673 are queued for more.
findings.proposal: Add one helper module next to whole_numbers.py, `solar_challenge/numbers.py`, with `require_finite(name, value, *, lo=None, hi=None, lo_open=False, hi_open=False) -> float`. It raises ConfigurationError/ValueError naming the field, the bound and the value (INV-2 style). Every frozen value type in this cluster calls it in __post_init__: SEGTariff, tariff.TariffPeriod, EventWindow, GridServicesEventsConfig, FlexibilityValueBand and FinanceConfig, whose hand-written loops it replaces. Parsers keep only type coercion. What becomes deletable: _parse_seg_rate_scalar's isfinite branch and the per-class hand-written comparisons. _NodeData and YearPoint keep their checks as the second, at-use enforcement point that heuristic 10 asks for, rather than as the only line of defence. This would have prevented the 374, 381, 652 and 656 sweep class, and it closes 382 and 673 in passing.

Measured: 2376 lines, 883 of them docstring and 205 comment (about 46% prose), leaving about 1012 code lines. Candidate partition with the heuristic-13 symptom for each.
