findings.title: The macro layer is bypassed: card, tab bar and form-label markup are repeated as long class-string literals, so every accessibility and layout fix is applied per instance
findings.statement: macros.html defines `card`, `stat_card`, `chart_container` and the badge macros, but the dominant structures are not routed through them. `card` is invoked once (dashboard.html), while the same card class triple (`bg-white dark:bg-slate-800 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-lg shadow-sm`) is written about 50 times across templates. The tab-button class string `border-primary-500 text-primary-600 dark:text-primary-400 ... border-transparent text-slate-500 ...` is copied into 10 buttons (results/home.html x4, results/fleet.html x3, history/compare.html x2, simulate/home.html x1). The pages have drifted apart: the results pages' tabs carry role='tab' and :aria-selected, compare.html's do not, and their padding and gap differ. The accessibility history shows the cost: 188 (dispatch select), 213 (sweep form, seven controls), 275 (fieldset/legend), 385 (distribution card, section captions) and 418 (row controls) each labelled controls one template at a time, and fix(138) and fix(288) repaired one layout at a time. A rule such as 'a tab list has role=tab and aria-selected' or 'a control has a label' lives nowhere a change can reach, so the next page repeats the gap. The remedy for drift so far has been tests that parse the markup (tests/_css_classes.py, tests/_html_page.py).
findings.proposal: Make the macros the only way these structures are written. Add `tab_bar(tabs, model='activeTab')` (renders role=tablist/tab, aria-selected, the active/inactive class pair once), a `panel(title, body)` built on `card`, and a `labelled_control(id, label, ...)` or `field(...)` for form controls whose label association is required by signature (the macro raises at render if no label is given). Convert results/home.html, fleet.html, compare.html, simulate/home.html and dashboard.html to them. Deletes about 50 card class literals, 10 tab class literals and the per-page tab markup. A 'no raw card or tab class string in page templates' test can then replace several parser-based guards. Prevents the a11y-per-control and layout-per-page fix classes (188, 213, 275, 385, 418, 138, 288).
findings.verdict_notes: The card macro is called once (dashboard.html:62) while the 'bg-white dark:bg-slate-800' card literal appears in about 15 templates, roughly 50 times in total. compare.html's tab buttons lack role/aria-selected.

findings.title: Template, CSS and class conventions are enforced by hand-written parsers of HTML, Jinja, Alpine, CSS and JS call sites in test helpers
findings.statement: tests/_css_classes.py (448 lines) is a CSS/Jinja/Alpine/inline-script reader: custom CSS block splitter (`_top_level_blocks`, `_lone_classes`, `_declarations`), CSS-escape handling, Alpine `:class` literal extraction, and Jinja AST walkers for `classes`/`_class` names. Its docstring lists two known unchecked gaps (classes returned from JS getters, and composed in other Jinja expressions). tests/_html_page.py (340 lines) reads page HTML plus regexes over inline script text for renderChart call sites (`render_chart_targets`, `_render_chart_call`, with a docstring about regular-expression literals). The theme and palette guards sit on top (test_web_theme_colours.py 316 lines, test_web_chart_colours.py 310, plus test_web_theme_palettes, test_web_compiled_css, test_web_hand_written_css, test_web_run_badges, test_web_inline_styles). The history shows this machinery being repeatedly repaired as a product: e828400 (blank CSS strings and url() tokens), e0b5b29 (declared_properties_by_class only inside @media/@supports/@layer), 467cee7 (case-insensitive property names), 2d9eb46, fd5dbd5/b0daf73 (function declaration read as a call), d41cef6 (class reader for {% set %}), a729e9a and d5aa3bb (guard premises). These are tests reaching into representation (heuristic 12 applied to tests, and the Tests stance): they pin how the source text is written rather than behaviour. A move of a role into a macro, or a restyle, requires editing allow-lists (_AMBER_ROLES lists template paths and class names). Most of this exists to compensate for the repeated-string design in the other findings.
findings.proposal: Treat the guards as a ratchet that should shrink as the structure improves. After the chart-description, palette and macro findings land, delete tests/unit/test_web_results_chart_targets.py, render_chart_targets/render_chart_figure, _AMBER_ROLES with its 4 tests, and the amber-copy premise check. Keep rendered-output tests (parse the response of the Flask test client with one real HTML parser, as server_drawn_badge already does) and the css-build lane. Do not add further regex/CSS parsers for new conventions. Encode each convention in a macro signature instead.
findings.bug_history_link: e828400, e0b5b29, 467cee7, 2d9eb46, fd5dbd5, b0daf73, d41cef6, a729e9a, d5aa3bb (parser/guard hardening amends); fix(356) class reader
findings.verdict_notes: The helper-based guard design is real, but the line counts, the fix-commit list and the claim that most of it compensates for the repeated-string design were not individually verified. It is a consequence of findings 2 and 6 rather than an independent defect, so the rating is low.

findings.title: dist/style.css freshness is checked only by a post-merge lane, so every template edit risks a red css-build fix task
findings.statement: static/dist/style.css is minified build output committed beside its sources, and Tailwind scans the raw text of templates and static/js, so any class-like token in a template, a JS string or a comment can change it. The invariant 'dist equals a fresh build of its sources' is enforced only by tests/css_build in the post-merge offline lane (needs npm and network). The per-task verify cannot run it. tests/unit/test_web_compiled_css.py covers only one direction (every applied class has some selector), so a removed class leaves a stale rule that nothing detects before merge (this is how 626 arose: task 363's server-rendered sidebar left two bare rules without a source). The result is a recurring file-and-fix cycle: 170, 222, 626, 634, 459 plus the licence-copy tasks 380/500/513, each a mechanical rebuild-and-commit. The agent that edits a template has no pre-merge signal that the artefact is stale.
findings.proposal: Make the check part of the task verify, offline: pre-seed an npm cache the way CLAUDE.md already does for uv, and run the same `npm ci --offline && npm run build:css` byte-for-byte comparison used by tests/css_build/test_dist_style_css.py as a non-slow test when node is available (skip with a loud message otherwise). Alternatively a pinned Tailwind standalone binary vendored in the repo. Deletes the post-merge fix-task round trip for CSS drift and the one-directional test_web_compiled_css guard. Reduces the number of tasks that touch dist/style.css after the fact.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(170) b4a9b02; fix(626) 7913162; 222 (css-build lane job); 634; 459; 380/500/513 licence copies
findings.verdict_notes: tests/css_build/test_dist_style_css.py exists and, per CLAUDE.md, runs only in the post-merge lane because it needs npm and network. tests/unit/test_web_compiled_css.py provides a partial pre-merge guard. The missing pre-merge freshness check is a deliberate offline-verify trade-off, and the task-number history was not verified.

findings.title: The lock sees a class only through inspect.signature plus body names, so every other contract dimension needs its own patch and several are unlocked
findings.statement: surface_form returns a string built from inspect.signature (or the Enum member list, or the constant's type name), and member_forms adds body names. Anything outside that lens is unpinned. I ran the helper on fixture classes (Python 3.14). A frozen dataclass and the same dataclass with frozen=False, order=True produce an identical surface_form ('(a: int, b: str = 'x') -> None') and an identical empty member_forms. This is live task 567; eq, unsafe_hash, slots and match_args are the same (task 668); the briefing's 'frozen but 9 are not' is task 669. A class with __slots__ gets a spurious member {'a': 'member_descriptor'}. A class constant is pinned only by type name ({'LIMIT': 'int', 'NAMES': 'tuple'}). A nested class is pinned as '()', with its own members unpinned. An Enum is pinned by iterating its members, so aliases are invisible (A=1, B=1 gives 'A=1, C=2'). Public module constants are pinned by type name alone in FROZEN_SURFACE: 'SEG_PRESETS': 'dict', 'OFGEM_TDCV_BY_OCCUPANTS': 'dict', 'SEASONAL_FACTORS': 'dict', 'ELEXON_PROFILE_CLASS_1': 'list', 'DEFAULT_EVENT_WINDOWS': 'tuple'. Deleting a preset key a consumer indexes passes the lock. Each dimension added so far arrived as a separate patch: members (404), instance attributes (426), settable properties (540), member order (583), and now 567/668/669. There is no per-class contract record, so each new dimension means a new function, a new guard and a new table convention.
findings.proposal: Make the unit of lock a structured, frozen per-name record instead of one string from one lens. Add `tests/_surface_forms.py::NameContract` with fields: kind, bases (names), constructor (signature form), `dataclass_options` (a frozen record of `cls.__dataclass_params__` frozen/eq/order/unsafe_hash/slots/match_args/kw_only, plus `__match_args__`), `members` (existing member_forms), and `value_digest` for public constants (a repr or sorted keys of the dict/list/tuple, so removing a key shows). `surface_form` stays as its constructor rendering. FROZEN_SURFACE and FROZEN_MEMBERS entries then become renderings of one record per name, compared field by field. A new contract dimension becomes one more field with one drift line, not a new function plus guard. Enum aliases (`__members__`), nested classes and slots get a single rule each inside that record. Tasks 567, 668 and 669 collapse into 'add fields to NameContract'. The bespoke member-order and settable-property conventions fold into the member field.
findings.bug_history_link: Live tasks 567 (frozen/order/eq flip uncaught), 668 (match_args/slots), 669 (briefing says frozen but 9 are not); earlier widenings 404, 426, 540, 583, 505 each added a dimension by patch
findings.verdict_notes: surface_form uses only inspect.signature, the Enum member list, or the constant's type name. Nothing in it or in tests/unit/test_public_api_surface.py (grep for frozen/__dataclass_params__ finds only prose) pins frozen/order/eq/slots. FROZEN_SURFACE pins constants like SEG_PRESETS as 'dict' and DEFAULT_EVENT_WINDOWS as 'tuple'.

findings.title: The annotation grammar is hardened for constructs the shipped library does not use, and each hardening adds code, tests and type-check ignores
findings.statement: The fail-closed contract of task 602 (a construct with no rule raises TypeError naming it) already makes the helper safe on any construct. Despite that, _parsed carries rules for InitVar, TypeVar/ParamSpec/TypeVarTuple (constraints, bound and default), NewType, Annotated, ParamSpec args/kwargs, the recursive-alias cut (_Evaluation, _Enclosing) and Callable parameter lists. I grepped src: the core modules contain no InitVar, NewType or Annotated (Annotated appears only in cli/), and TypeVars only privately (config._Built); the only alias is heart_pump HeatPumpType = Literal[...]. A line trace of the helper over the real surface (69 forms, 8 closure classes, all members of every pinned class) executed 157 of 211 statements. The unexecuted ones are the InitVar branch of _parsed, _parsed_type_variable, _parsed_new_type, _Declared, _Keyword, _ParameterTypes.text, the Annotated branch and the recursion cut in _Unevaluated.classes. The fix tasks 546, 551, 588 (InitVar), 608 (TypeVar/NewType), 617 (forward reference in its own evaluation), 630 and 631 all harden those paths. The 631 fix exists only because the helper reads TypeVar.__default__ and NewType.__qualname__, which typeshed does not declare on every minor, hence the `# type: ignore[union-attr]` and `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` and live task 644 (unused ignores). In test_surface_forms_helper.py, 21 of 94 tests (about 300 of 1,099 test lines) are about InitVar, NewType, TypeVar, ParamSpec, Unpack or self-referential declarations. This is the 12-of-18 'one construct per fix' pattern the mined themes read as 'each new annotation in src triggers a fix'. In fact no src annotation triggered any of them.
findings.proposal: Shrink _parsed to the vocabulary the library actually uses (classes, unions, generics/subscriptions, Literal, ClassVar, strings and forward references, None, bare typing aliases, special forms) and let everything else keep raising the existing TypeError from task 602. Delete `_parsed_type_variable`, `_parsed_new_type`, `_Declared`, `_Keyword`, the InitVar branch plus `_init_only_variables`, the `_Enclosing` TypeVar/NewType members, the typeshed-gap ignores (and so the 631/644 class), and the 21 matching tests. Keep one test pinning that an unmodelled construct raises. When src first uses a construct, the TypeError names it and a task adds one rule driven by a real signature. The `_Evaluation` cut stays only if a real self-referential alias appears. A removed rule can be re-added from git history when needed.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(546)/(551)/(588) InitVar, fix(608) TypeVar/NewType, fix(617) forward reference in own evaluation, fix(631) typeshed getattr, live 644 unused type-ignore and 670 file size (1,454 lines)
findings.verdict_notes: Grep of src outside cli/ finds no InitVar or NewType. TypeVars are private (config._Built and the web modules). The helper carries _parsed_type_variable, _parsed_new_type, _Declared, _Keyword, and tests/unit/test_surface_forms_helper.py is 1454 lines. The 157-of-211 trace and the live task numbers were not re-run, but the structural claim holds. It is not wrong to harden a fail-closed lock; the cost is the real point.

findings.title: The frozen text depends on source style: the same type is spelled differently by future-annotations modules, quoting and runtime evaluation
findings.statement: _Unevaluated.text() returns the annotation string as written, while _Unevaluated.classes() evaluates it. So one grammar produces two different readings of one annotation. The result is that form depends on a source-style switch, not on the type. I ran surface_form on two equivalent modules. With `from __future__ import annotations`, `def f(a: Optional[A], b: A | None, c: "Optional[A]")` is spelled '(a: Optional[A], b: A | None, c: 'Optional[A]')'. Without it, the same def is spelled '(a: A | None, b: A | None, c: Optional[A])'. FROZEN_SURFACE shows the effect directly: finance.py, community.py and optimize.py (future-annotations modules) appear as `Optional[BatteryConfig]` and `'FinanceConfig'` (quotes included), while pv.py and load.py appear as `dict[str, float] | None`. Adding or removing the future import, or re-quoting an annotation, changes the frozen text of every name in a module with no API change. That fails the lock and triggers the table-edit and release-note ceremony. Ruff selects only `F`, so no pyupgrade rewrite forces this today, but any sweep like task 493's can. The helper already evaluates every string on the real surface to find classes, so the canonical reading exists.
findings.proposal: Make `_Unevaluated.text()` spell the evaluated annotation (`_parsed(_evaluated(source, module), enclosing | {evaluation}).text()`), keeping the written source only for the recursion cut. Then Optional[X], X | None, 'X' and X all render alike on every minor, and `from __future__` and quoting stop mattering. `text()` and `classes()` come from one reading, and the `_Evaluation` cut becomes the only place a string is spelled as written. Regenerate FROZEN_SURFACE, FROZEN_CLOSURE and FROZEN_MEMBERS once, in one commit with a release note saying spelling only. The `Optional['GridServicesEventsConfig']` style entries go away.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (no commit has yet hit it); the frozen tables mix Optional[...] and | None entries today, and fix(617)/amend 4f95d0b show string evaluation is where the helper's bugs concentrate
findings.verdict_notes: finance.py, community.py and optimize.py have `from __future__ import annotations`; pv.py and load.py do not. FROZEN_SURFACE mixes `Optional[...]`, quoted names and `| None`. For example, FinanceConfig is frozen as `Optional[float]` and `Optional['GridServicesEventsConfig']`, while SummaryStatistics uses `float | None`. The text depends on source style. Speculative in practice, but real.

findings.title: The release-note obligation that makes a table edit legitimate is only prose in an assertion message
findings.statement: The briefing and _drift_message state that every edit to FROZEN_SURFACE, FROZEN_CLOSURE or FROZEN_MEMBERS needs an 'Unreleased on main' line in docs/domain-library-consumption.md in the same commit. I grepped tests/: the string appears in no test other than inside that message. tests/unit/test_consumption_doc.py contains one test that the doc exists. The workflow is: the failure prints the current form 'ready to paste', the agent pastes it, the test is green. The only gate that distinguishes an acknowledged break from a silent one is a reviewer noticing a missing doc line. The lock also does not classify drift. A removed or retyped parameter (breaking) and an appended defaulted parameter (additive) print the same way, though the forms are structured enough to tell them apart.
findings.proposal: Add an `UNRELEASED_SINCE_TAG: dict[str, int]` table in test_public_api_surface.py mapping each pinned path (name, class, or class.member) whose form differs from the 0.5.0 tag to its task id, and a test asserting each id appears in an 'Unreleased on main' line of docs/domain-library-consumption.md and each such line cites an id in the table. Have `_drift_message` also label a drifted entry as 'additive' or 'breaking' from the structured record in finding 1 (removed name or parameter, retyped parameter, new parameter without default). This turns the prose obligation into an executable one at the same single point where the tables are edited.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; 20+ 'Unreleased on main' lines exist today (tasks 392, 505, 426, 540, ...), kept by convention
findings.verdict_notes: 'Unreleased on main' appears in tests only inside message strings (test_public_api_surface.py lines ~201 and ~523). tests/unit/test_consumption_doc.py has no check for it. The obligation is prose only, and drift is not classified as breaking or additive.

findings.title: The attributes-set-on-self guard hard-codes the receiver name and descends into nested classes
findings.statement: _attributes_set_on_self walks the whole class source with ast.walk and matches `Attribute(value=Name(id='self'), ctx=Store())` and the literal `object.__setattr__(self, '<const>', ...)`. I ran it on a fixture. An attribute set by a nested helper class (`class _Helper: def __init__(self): self.leaked = 1`) is attributed to the outer class: undeclared_attributes reported {'leaked'} and also {'ok'} for the outer. A @staticmethod whose first parameter happens to be named self (`self.fromstatic = 1`) is counted. Setting through any other receiver name (`def configure(this, v): this.renamed = v`), `setattr(self, 'x', v)` or `self.__dict__['x'] = v` is missed silently. The home.py SimulationResults case (`object.__setattr__(self, name, series.rename(column))` in a loop) already shows non-constant names occur in pinned classes; there they are declared fields, so the guard passes by luck. The guard enforces the 'declare every attribute you set' invariant of task 426, so a miss lets an unpinned public attribute escape the member lock.
findings.proposal: Scan each function defined directly in the class body (not nested ClassDef) and take its receiver as the first parameter of any non-static method. Collect Store targets on that name, plus constant-name setattr/__setattr__ on it. Fail closed with a TypeError on a non-constant setattr or `__dict__` write on the receiver, naming the class, since the guard cannot tell what it sets. Add the three fixtures above to test_surface_forms_helper.py.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; guard introduced by task 426, widened by 551 (init-only variables) and 550
findings.verdict_notes: The code ast.walks the whole dedented class source and matches only Name(id='self') stores and the object.__setattr__(self, const, ...) call. It therefore descends into nested classes and staticmethods whose first parameter is named self, and it misses other receiver names, setattr and __dict__. The impact is limited (low severity): a miss weakens the declare-every-attribute guard only.

findings.title: The helper keeps process-global state keyed by module name and detects generated __init__ by a CPython artefact
findings.statement: _type_checking_imports is `functools.cache`d on the module name string, and _evaluated resolves that name through sys.modules and re-execs the imports on every evaluation. The cache outlives a module reload or a different module reusing the name, and the contract leaks into the tests. The docstring of the test helper `_imported` says 'Give each test's module a name no other test uses: the helper under test reads a module's `if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports once per name'. Test authors must know an internal cache to write a correct fixture (the Tests stance: a seam leaking implementation). Separately, _holds_generated_init decides that an __init__ was generated by dataclasses via `init.__code__.co_qualname != init.__qualname__`, an artefact of how CPython's dataclasses compiles and renames the function. It works across the admitted minors today (the interpreter matrix is green) but rests on no documented behaviour. Task 620 and commits 8fe3d5b/65c0893 show it was already revised twice. A change in how dataclasses builds __init__ would silently make inherited fields evaluate in the wrong module, and the NameError would surface as an opaque lock failure.
findings.proposal: Key the TYPE_CHECKING-import cache on the module object (or the code object of its source) and return a fresh namespace per module. Alternatively drop the cache, since the real surface has few modules and parsing is cheap. Then delete the 'unique module name' obligation from `_imported`. Replace the co_qualname test with a positive check made at decoration time: compare `vars(cls)['__init__']` against `cls.__dataclass_params__.init` plus whether the class body's own AST defines `__init__` (the helper already parses class source in `_attributes_set_on_self`). The decision is then derived from source, not from a compiler artefact.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(620) and amend 8fe3d5b/65c0893 (the 'generated __init__' module decision revised three times)
findings.verdict_notes: _type_checking_imports is @functools.cache keyed on the module name string. _holds_generated_init compares init.__code__.co_qualname with init.__qualname__, a CPython artefact that the docstring itself describes.

findings.title: The public name list is restated in four places in __init__.py and a literal 69 in five more, with tests reaching the private tables
findings.statement: Each of the 69 public names is declared in __all__, in _SYMBOL_MODULE, in the TYPE_CHECKING import block and in FROZEN_SURFACE. The one alias additionally sits in _SOURCE_NAME. The literal 69 is restated in test_public_api_surface.py (docstring, comment, `len(...) == len(FROZEN_SET) == 69`, message), test_init_lazy_surface.py (`assert len(as_list) == 69`) and the briefing. The sync between __all__ and _SYMBOL_MODULE is an import-time RuntimeError, and the other pairs are separate tests. test_every_name_resolves_and_caches reads `solar_challenge._SYMBOL_MODULE` and `_SOURCE_NAME` with `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`, so the lazy-loader test pins private tables. Per the briefing the sync check, the RuntimeError, the lazy loader and the DispatchTariffPeriod alias are intentional.
findings.proposal: Keep every guard the briefing protects. Reduce the restatements by folding `_SOURCE_NAME` into the origin table, as `_ORIGIN: dict[str, tuple[str, str]]` mapping public name to (module, source name). `__getattr__` and `__dir__` use it, and the import-time RuntimeError still compares its keys with the literal `__all__`, which static consumers read. Drop the numeric 69 from the tests (the duplicate check is `len(__all__) == len(set(__all__))`, and set equality with FROZEN_SET covers the rest). The test then drives public behaviour (`getattr(solar_challenge, name) is getattr(import_module(origin), source)`) with FROZEN_SURFACE's keys and the TYPE_CHECKING ast check, not by reaching `_SYMBOL_MODULE`.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; briefing warns against tidying the sync check and the alias away
findings.verdict_notes: The restatement is real: __all__, _SYMBOL_MODULE, the TYPE_CHECKING block, and FROZEN_SURFACE. The literal 69 is repeated in the tests. tests/unit/test_init_lazy_surface.py lines 52-53 read the private tables with type: ignore. It is overstated, though. __all__ and _SYMBOL_MODULE are guarded by an import-time RuntimeError, the other pairs by tests, and the duplication is intentional (it supports the lazy loader and the typed surface for mypy) and drift-guarded. Low severity.

findings.title: Dependency floors have no lower-bound probe; each is discovered by an incident and justified only in hand-written prose tables
findings.statement: The invariant 'every release a declared floor admits works with this code' is checked nowhere, and the lock hides it. uv.lock pins every direct dependency far above its floor: pandas>=2.0.0 against 3.0.3, mypy>=1.0.0 against 2.1.0, pytest>=7.0.0 against 9.0.3, typer>=0.12.1 against 0.26.3, playwright>=1.51.0 against 1.61.0, scipy>=1.7.2 against 1.17.1. The lanes probe the locked set (verify, interpreter matrix) and the newest set (newest-releases), but never the oldest. A consumer that re-locks, or pip install '.[e2e]', can land on a floor release that nothing has run. Floors therefore get found when something breaks, and each find is encoded once as a RED test. test_e2e_extra and test_build_system hold a table of (distribution, first_capable_release, capability) whose 'capability' is a prose claim that the e2e tests or pyproject use some API. Nothing verifies that claim or that tests/e2e still calls the API, so the table can drift silently. The two test bodies are the same declared_floor assertion copied (live task 657), and the dev and runtime floors have no such test at all (live task 655, the mypy floor). Only the floors that have already bitten are guarded: setuptools 62.3 and 77, playwright 1.44 and 1.51, pytest-playwright 0.5 and 0.6.
findings.proposal: Add a lowest-direct lane job, 'oldest-releases'. It runs the same pattern as tests/newest_releases: copy_working_tree, then `uv lock --resolution lowest-direct` in a scratch copy, sync every extra, then run_verify_suite on the pin. A red there files a fix task naming the node-id and the floor to raise, exactly as the newest-releases job does for upstream moves. Give it a LANE_JOBS row with the shared LaneContract set. The floor then derives from an executed probe, which is the single point of truth, and test_e2e_extra's and test_build_system's capability tables become deletable. Keep only the generic invariant that a floor exists for every direct dependency, in one parametrised test that replaces the copied bodies (657). Fixing a failing oldest-release run raises the floor in pyproject.toml, and the same run would have surfaced 251, 258, 292, 589, 471 and 655 before a consumer did. Expect to raise several stale floors on the first run; that is the finding materialising, not a regression.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(251) setuptools>=62.3.0; fix(258) setuptools>=77.0.0 and SPDX licence; fix(292) playwright>=1.51.0; fix(589) pytest-playwright>=0.6.0; feat(471) typer help rendering; live tasks 655 (mypy floor admits failing releases) and 657 (floor-contract bodies copied three times)
findings.verdict_notes: Verified. pyproject.toml declares pandas>=2.0.0, typer>=0.12.1, pytest>=7.0.0 and mypy>=1.0.0. The only floor tests are tests/unit/test_e2e_extra.py and tests/unit/test_build_system.py, which use tests/_pyproject.py::declared_floor. Each is a table of prose 'capability' claims that nothing checks against tests/e2e, followed by the same declared_floor assertion. No test covers dev or runtime floors, and no lowest-direct probe exists. Severity 'high' is overstated; the gap is real.

findings.title: 'Run a configured command as the orchestrator runs it' is recomposed at every call site from command, cwd, env and runner
findings.statement: The orchestrator runs a configured command by looking it up (a verify slot key or a lane job name), joining the job's cwd onto the worktree root, running it under sh -c in an environment with no caller virtualenv or uv lock mode, and optionally collect-only. The tests rebuild this composition at five sites. collect_lane_job composes sole_offline_lane_job, lane_job_directory and run_collect_only(env=). test_each_lane_job_refuses_a_stale_lock_naming_uv_lock repeats the same trio by hand. test_per_task_verify._collect_with_test_command pairs load_orchestrator_config()['test_command'] with run_collect_only. test_the_verify_refuses_a_stale_lock_naming_uv_lock indexes config[key] itself. run_verify_suite reads test_command and then uses a separate Popen runner. Every omission has been a bug. fix(273) found a probe that ignored the job's cwd. fix(344) found probes sharing the caller's .venv and lock mode. fix(309) found a plain `uv run` silently re-locking. Each was fixed at one site while the others kept their own composition. The two runners also differ: run_verify_suite runs in its own session and killpg's the group on timeout, but run_collect_only uses subprocess.run(shell=True, timeout=300), which kills only the shell. The environment is a denylist of four names (VIRTUAL_ENV, UV_FROZEN, UV_LOCKED, UV_NO_SYNC), so any other ambient UV_* setting leaks into a probe that is supposed to model a clean lane.
findings.proposal: Introduce a frozen `OrchestratorCommand` in tests/_orchestrator_config.py, built by `verify_command(project_root, slot)` or `lane_command(project_root, name)`. It carries the command string and the cwd rule. A single `run(root, env, *, collect_only_args=(), timeout=..., new_session=...)` is the only place that applies cwd, the process-group discipline and the collect-only PYTEST_ADDOPTS. collect_lane_job, the two stale-lock tests, _collect_with_test_command and run_verify_suite all become one-line calls, and run_collect_only and run_verify_suite stop being separate runners. Make `isolated_uv_env` an allowlist or an explicit 'lane environment' constructor (PATH, HOME and the UV_ cache keys), so a new caller-side uv switch cannot leak in. A new lane job or slot then cannot be probed without its cwd and environment, which closes the 273, 344 and 309 class.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(273) interpreter-matrix probe ignored the job's cwd; fix(344) lane-job collect probes in a fresh isolated env; fix(309) verify and lane run uv run --locked
findings.verdict_notes: The runner and env pieces are already shared (run_collect_only, isolated_uv_env). The real repeated composition is sole_offline_lane_job + lane_job_directory + run_collect_only, in tests/_lane_collection.py::collect_lane_job and in tests/unit/test_stale_uv_lock.py::test_each_lane_job_refuses_a_stale_lock_naming_uv_lock (3 lines). tests/unit/test_per_task_verify.py::_collect_with_test_command is a different lookup (test_command). The 'five sites' figure is overstated. The runner difference is real: tests/_verify_suite.py::run_verify_suite uses Popen with start_new_session and killpg, while tests/_collect_only.py::run_collect_only uses subprocess.run(shell=True, timeout=300). The denylist of four env names in tests/_uv_env.py is real.

findings.title: The offline guard's exemption is keyed on two overloaded marks, so the 'non-slow e2e tests need no network' contract is assumed, not enforced
findings.statement: Three independent axes are carried by two marks. The axes are lane membership (what runs in the verify), network permission (what the guard exempts) and browser dependency. e2e means 'deselected from the verify' and also 'exempt from the offline guard'. slow means 'needs a live service' and also 'exempt'. The e2e lane runs `-m 'not slow'`, so its contract is that every unmarked test works without a live service. The guard cannot check that, because every e2e-marked test is exempt wholesale. The e2e row of LANE_JOBS lists only COLLECTS_ONLY_ITS_SUITE. The session's JobManager (_e2e_job_manager) is the real one with the real simulate_home. Non-slow tests such as test_home_simulation's form-submission tests POST to the live server and start real jobs that fetch PVGIS; only release_held_simulations, used by test_parameter_sweep, swaps in a stub. This is why task 366 (non-slow e2e fetches live PVGIS) and the e2e lane fix tasks 357 and 508 exist, and why the lane depends on PVGIS being up. The e2e mark is also hand-applied as a per-module `pytestmark` in 23 modules. No contract test asserts that a module under tests/e2e carries it, although the same conftest already iterates all items under its directory to add the flaky marker.
findings.proposal: Split the axes. Apply the e2e mark centrally, in tests/e2e/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems beside the flaky marker, and delete the 23 `pytestmark` lines. Drop 'e2e' from _MARKS_OF_TESTS_ALLOWED_ONLINE so only slow exempts. Give `_e2e_job_manager` a deterministic `simulate_home` stub by default, the constructor argument release_held_simulations already uses, so non-slow e2e tests keep the guard's in-process socket refusal (the live server runs in a thread of the pytest process, so the patch applies). Add `EVERY_TEST_OFFLINE_OR_SLOW` to LaneContract for the e2e row. The 'no live service without a slow mark' contract is then enforced for the one suite where it was only assumed, and 366, 387 and 624 stop being possible. Whether Chromium honours the proxy variables is a separate question, so the in-process refusal is the enforcement point.
findings.bug_history_link: live tasks 366 and 387 (non-slow e2e tests fetch live PVGIS), 357 and 508 (offline-lane e2e fix tasks), 624 (blocked pvgis lane fix); fix(147) and fix(131) e2e live-server and JobManager draining
findings.verdict_notes: tests/conftest.py::_MARKS_OF_TESTS_ALLOWED_ONLINE = ('slow','e2e'), so any e2e-marked test skips the offline guard. The LANE_JOBS e2e row lists only COLLECTS_ONLY_ITS_SUITE. The non-slow e2e lane contract is therefore not enforced by the guard. tests/e2e/conftest.py::_e2e_job_manager is the real session manager, with only release_held_simulations as a stub path. The e2e mark is applied per module via pytestmark, and no contract test asserts it. I did not trace that the form-submission jobs actually reach PVGIS.

findings.title: 'Lane-only suite' is expressed by two mechanisms, and the e2e suite, the one with the older mechanism, is outside the default-collection contract
findings.statement: Three lane suites (interpreter_matrix, css_build, newest_releases) are kept out of default collections by tests/conftest.py::collect_ignore, which an explicit path overrides. LaneContract.NEVER_IN_A_DEFAULT_COLLECTION checks it with addopts cleared. The fourth lane suite, tests/e2e, is kept out by three restatements: pyproject.toml's addopts `--ignore=tests/e2e`, test_command's `--ignore=tests/e2e`, and `-m 'not slow and not e2e'`. Its LANE_JOBS row does not list NEVER_IN_A_DEFAULT_COLLECTION. A default collection with addopts cleared, which dark-factory's serial and confirm reruns append (per the _lane_collection docstring), would reach tests/e2e and fail on `from playwright...` imports with no contract test noticing, the failure fix 3d7474f recorded when a bare pytest was interrupted across all 1084 tests. The redundancy is deliberate (heuristic 10 asks for redundant enforcement). The defect is that the definition of 'lane-only' has no single home, and one member has no checking test.
findings.proposal: Add 'e2e' to tests/conftest.py::collect_ignore (the tests/e2e conftest then never loads in default collections, and an explicit `pytest tests/e2e` still collects it, as for the other three suites). Add NEVER_IN_A_DEFAULT_COLLECTION to the e2e LANE_JOBS row. Then the addopts `--ignore` and test_command's `--ignore=tests/e2e` become redundant belt-and-braces that the contract test keeps honest, rather than the only line of defence. Derive the ignore list from LANE_JOBS (the `suite` field) if a table row can be read at conftest import time without a cycle.
findings.bug_history_link: fix 3d7474f 'skip e2e test collection when playwright is not installed'; feat(222) and feat(471) each added a collect_ignore entry by hand; speculative for a regression on the serial-rerun path
findings.verdict_notes: collect_ignore lists only interpreter_matrix, css_build and newest_releases. tests/e2e is excluded by pyproject addopts --ignore=tests/e2e and the test_command. The LANE_JOBS e2e row in tests/unit/test_offline_lane_contracts.py omits NEVER_IN_A_DEFAULT_COLLECTION. tests/e2e/conftest.py guards only werkzeug via importorskip. The claim is real but speculative and low-severity, as the finding itself says.

findings.title: Tests restate dark-factory's lane semantics and defaults (cwd, enabled coercion, seam defaults) because the orchestrator exposes no validator
findings.statement: The upstream subsystem is the dark-factory orchestrator. Its pydantic LaneCommand model (cwd: str = '.', enabled: bool, command run via sh -c with DF_VERIFY_ROLE=offline) already validates this config on load. This repo cannot import that model, so it re-implements the rules by hand with asserts: lane_job_directory (cwd is a str that resolves to a directory) and lane_job_enabled (a YAML boolean), each citing dark-factory's config.py path in its docstring. It also pins defaults the orchestrator should not apply to a project at all. dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml must set offline_lane_infra_enabled: false and offline_lane_legacy_numeric_enabled: false explicitly, because those default-on seams run scripts/run-offline-deep.sh and reify's tests/infra/run_all.sh, which this repo lacks, and `when unset it is on if dark-factory's default ever is` (fix 304 folding 305). The missing upstream guarantees are a project-config validation entry point and a seam default that does not presume the project has the seam script. Meanwhile run_collect_only models the lane env only by what it removes, and omits DF_VERIFY_ROLE=offline, so the model can diverge from the lane silently.
findings.proposal: Upstream, in dark-factory: expose `orchestrator validate-config <path>` (or a documented schema) that loads the file through OrchestratorConfig and prints each job's resolved command, cwd, enabled flag and env keys, and make the legacy numeric and infra seams default off unless their script exists. Here, make tests/_orchestrator_config.py shell out to that resolver, or read its JSON, once per session. lane_job_directory and lane_job_enabled and their assertions become deletable, and the two explicit `: false` lines plus their pinning test stop being needed. Until the upstream entry point exists, keep the helpers but record the dependency in one place, as a docs/ pointer, instead of per-function docstrings.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(304) offline_lane_infra_enabled set explicitly (folds 305); fix(273) lane probe cwd rule; speculative for further orchestrator-default drift
findings.verdict_notes: Verified in-repo: lane_job_directory and lane_job_enabled hand-validate lane config, and dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml sets offline_lane_infra_enabled and offline_lane_legacy_numeric_enabled to false, asserted in tests/unit/test_offline_lane_contracts.py. DF_VERIFY_ROLE appears nowhere in the repo, so run_collect_only does not model it. The upstream-gap claim (a pydantic LaneCommand model, seam defaults) is outside this tree and unverified. Explicitly pinning false is arguably the correct h10 practice, not a defect. The finding is mostly speculative about upstream.

findings.title: Operational rationale, measured timings and the lane command lists are prose in the YAML, CLAUDE.md and test docstrings, with timeout relations asserted only in comments
findings.statement: Comments stance. 85 of dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml's 134 lines are comments, about 63% of the file. They carry measurements that go stale (the e2e timeout is '~8x the measured 214 s run', pvgis 'measures ~20 s', css-build '17-38 s by host load', newest-releases '17-19 min') and the lane-job intent that CLAUDE.md and each lane test module's docstring restate. The literal lane commands, with their `--extra` sets, appear in CLAUDE.md eleven times as well as in the YAML, with no test tying the two together. Timeouts are likewise spread across the YAML command prefixes (`timeout -k 60 1800`, `600`), _SUITE_TIMEOUT_SECS=7200 'about 15x the slowest measured run (491 s on 3.11)', _UV_TIMEOUT_SECS=900, _NPM_TIMEOUT_SECS=120 and run_collect_only's 300. The css_build comment asserts 'both npm steps' timeouts together fit inside the css-build job's timeout', and the unmarked jobs 'have no timeout: its suite timeout bounds a hang'. Those are relations between constants in different files that nothing checks. Part of this was already rehomed: amend a79a410 moved the lint rationale into docs/lint-gate.md and 6c1e31b dropped copied values.
findings.proposal: Finish the rehoming. Move the per-job intent, measurements and fix-task conventions into one tracked doc, docs/offline-lane.md, which the YAML points at in one line and CLAUDE.md summarises without restating the commands. Delete the measured-number sentences, or keep them only in the commit message. Make the timeout relation a checked invariant instead of a comment: derive the wrapper figures from LANE_JOBS (a `timeout_secs` field per row) and assert in the lane contract tests that each suite's internal timeouts sum to less than its job timeout.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; the amend volume on dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml (6c1e31b, a79a410, d016cf2 'correct the stale web-extra rationale') shows the prose drifting
findings.verdict_notes: The file is 134 lines, 85 of them comment lines, and it carries measured timings ('17-38 s', '17-19 min'). Timeouts are spread: 'timeout -k 60 1800' and 'timeout -k 60 600' in the YAML, plus constants in tests/. The relations between those constants are stated in comments only. Real but low-severity; the finding admits some rehoming already happened.

findings.title: Lane probes read pytest's text listing, by substring and by splitting node ids on brackets
findings.statement: The lane contract tests need typed facts about a collection: node id, test file, marks and parametrisation id. They derive them by parsing pytest's text output. collected_node_ids keeps every stdout line containing '::', so any warning or uv line that contains '::' reads as a test. _lies_under partitions the id on '::'. _interpreters_named_by does `node_id.rpartition('[')[2].removesuffix(']')` to recover a parametrise id. The mode itself travels through PYTEST_ADDOPTS and depends on an undocumented ini -v cancelling -q (test_collect_only pins it). test_per_task_verify has already moved to a structured form, a JUnit XML report, for the skip question. So there are two ways of reading a collection, one structured and one parsed, and the hotspot's fix history is dominated by the lane harness diverging from the real lane.
findings.proposal: Write a small `-p tests._collection_report` plugin, placed on PYTHONPATH by run_collect_only, whose pytest_collection_finish hook dumps `[{nodeid, path, marks, callspec_id}]` as JSON to a file named by an environment variable. run_collect_only then returns a typed `Collection` (tuple of frozen `CollectedTest`). collected_node_ids, _lies_under, _interpreters_named_by (it reads callspec_id) and the '::' filter all die. suite_node_ids_matching becomes a filter on `marks` instead of re-running pytest with `-m`.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative
findings.verdict_notes: collected_node_ids returns every stdout line containing '::'. tests/unit/test_interpreter_matrix_lane.py::_interpreters_named_by does node_id.rpartition('[')[2].removesuffix(']'). tests/unit/test_per_task_verify.py already uses a --junitxml report for the skip question, so two readings of a collection coexist. Real, low-severity.

The same pattern appears in HeatPumpConfig, EVConfig, Location.altitude (pv-weather.8 (fk-7dcdc5559d22)), 21 dispatch.py guards (home-battery-dispatch.1 (fk-a9c609ecb8ef)), and EventWindow, GridServicesEventsConfig and FlexibilityValueBand (finance-projection.7 (fk-b69968a37b36)). The patches went in downstream, one area at a time. In the web layer, number_fields was built and fleet_config rebuilds config's whole grammar so it can reach the numbers (web-form-parsing.1 (fk-60410de6dd0a)); fleet_scenario._read_fleet_size_and_seed pre-reads n_homes and seed ahead of config's int(); api.simulate_sweep and assistant.py still forgot (web-form-parsing.4 (fk-bea05911eb70), live 440). In config, parse_seg_rate_scalar checks isfinite before building SEGTariff, which only covers YAML. In finance, _NodeData and YearPoint guard the end of the pipeline (652, 656). In the domain, guards were added class by class (332, 378, 384, 590, 633). Errors are split too. Domain classes raise ValueError with no key path. Config raises ConfigurationError, which is defined in config.py above finance and gridservices, so those modules use 11 function-local imports to break the cycle (scenario-config.6 (fk-4435376bedb3) and finance-projection.6 (fk-4435376bedb3) are one root cause seen from two clusters). Web endpoints each catch whichever (ValueError, TypeError) their own coercions raise (web-jobs-runs.7 (fk-239274130a5a)). web-form-parsing.3 (fk-9dd1d9389dd2) is what this structure produced. The 312 bound was applied in fleet_config._pool_counts only, so builder validation still builds a 10**12-element shuffled pool. Merges: scenario-config.6 (fk-4435376bedb3) with finance-projection.6 (fk-4435376bedb3) (the ConfigurationError location). web-form-parsing.4 (fk-bea05911eb70)'s SweepRequest with web-jobs-runs.7 (fk-239274130a5a)'s SweepRequest (the same typed request record).
chains.proposal: Add one leaf module, solar_challenge/quantities.py, beside whole_numbers.py and absorbing it. It provides require_finite(name, value, lo, hi, open/closed), require_whole(name, value, lo, hi) and require_bool, refuses bool-as-number, and raises ValueError naming the quantity, the value and the bound. Every domain __post_init__ calls it: PV, Battery, Load, HeatPump, EV, Location, the dispatch decision and strategies, EnergyFlowResult, SEGTariff, TariffPeriod, EventWindow, GridServicesEventsConfig, FlexibilityValueBand, FinanceConfig and the distribution types. Move ConfigurationError to a leaf errors.py and make it subclass ValueError. It is in neither __all__ nor FROZEN_CLOSURE (verified), so the move needs no bump. Above that, scenario_fields.py provides path-carrying readers and one build(block_path, Cls, fields) boundary that re-raises domain errors as ConfigurationError with the key path. Config's block readers and distribution builders use it. web/number_fields becomes a thin adapter, and the web request records (SweepRequest etc.) read through it. The web pre-reads, _spec_number/_other_setting and the per-endpoint except blocks then become deletable. Separately and now, bound the builder's shuffled-pool counts (web-form-parsing.3 (fk-9dd1d9389dd2)), and bound pool total against n_homes inside config. Refusing NaN on a public constructor is a behaviour change for the consumer, so it needs an 'Unreleased on main' line. No signature changes.

chains.name: Physics results drop provenance (was it priced, which kWh were PV vs grid charge, what SOC envelope applied), so finance and charts re-infer it from totals
chains.description: Defect: simulate_home encodes 'no tariff' as a priced £0 and keeps only money totals. flow.py computes pv_charge_stored_kwh and grid_charge_stored_kwh per step, but SummaryStatistics carries only total_grid_charge_kwh. The SoH-derated SOC envelope exists only on a live, mutable Battery. Downstream patches, one per consumer: finance._physics_import_cost_gbp infers 'unpriced' from `== 0.0 and > 0.0` (8dffcf8, 307, live 690). householder_bill and _seg_export_income_gbp back-derive unit rates, and a zero-physics-export home loses its SEG; a test pins that loss through private names. charts._unpriced_import_note infers the same fact from tariff_rate.gt(0), its docstring admitting it 'cannot tell' (665: three commits and an amend). sankey_diagram and comparison_radar re-derive the PV/grid charge split differently (469, 492, 628). battery_soc_chart and gridservices.compute_fleet_spare_capacity_kw construct throwaway Batteries to read limits (645). The grid-charge controller is fed nominal capacity (632). The two flow paths duplicate the settle tail and feed compute_grid_charge_power_kw different SOC bases (home-battery-dispatch.3 (fk-4df47ebe6a96), live 270). The finance ledger split (finance-projection.2 (fk-caeaf35c8151): bill and CBS revenue assembled twice, with no balance invariant) produced the 219, 271, 281, 307 and 308 class, the same disagreement one layer up. Merges: finance-projection.1 (fk-52fa98174363)'s FlowPricing with web-templates-theme.3 (fk-8e109704aa24)'s tariff_configured/seg_configured are one missing fact, so give it one record. home-battery-dispatch.2 (fk-f126b1c9cbbe)'s SocEnvelope with web-templates-theme.3 (fk-8e109704aa24)'s soc_limits_kwh are one value.
chains.proposal: Make flow.py's single _settle(...) the only producer of derived per-step flows, including the PV and grid charge split (home-battery-dispatch.3 (fk-4df47ebe6a96)). Then carry three typed facts across the physics-to-consumer boundary. (1) A FlowPricing record: import_priced, flow-weighted import rate, and the SEG rate from HomeConfig.seg_tariff. (2) total_pv_charge_kwh beside total_grid_charge_kwh. (3) The SocEnvelope value built once in battery.py, which the results record. Results should carry the envelope rather than charts rebuilding it from config, because the platform assigns min_soc_fraction at runtime. On top of that, finance builds one frozen HomeLedger per home, with own_use + import == demand enforced in __post_init__. householder_bill and _simulate_age both sum ledgers. Charts read the typed fields, and compare.html draws through renderChart. This is a frozen-contract change: SummaryStatistics is in __all__ and SimulationResults is in FROZEN_CLOSURE, and the briefing calls adding a public member breaking. It therefore needs a deliberate version/tag bump, batched with the other bump-requiring remedies, and lands after surface-lock.1 (fk-879e8c13f581)'s NameContract.

chains.name: config.py keeps the fleet-distribution parser and sampler private, so the web layer re-implements grammar, sampler and importer in two server decoders and two page scripts
chains.description: Defect: _parse_distribution_spec, _sample_from_distribution and _DistributionSampler are private, and config's distribution layer restates component defaults (scenario-config.2 (fk-148991ab9439)). The web layer therefore keeps its own copies. The preview samples through fleet_config._draw_samples, which accepts normal min>max and negative weights that config refuses (live 569, 571). Two wire encodings of one editor state have two decoders with different defaults and bounds: the fleet page runs {type: normal} as N(0,1), while the builder refuses it (web-form-parsing.2 (fk-a6d9f3e5a7e2), live 313). Two scenario-to-form importers follow opposite policies, one on the server and one in js-yaml in the browser (web-form-parsing.7 (fk-40dff1473b94), live 298, 545, 549, 553, 554). fleet_config's lossy rebuild hides misspelt keys from config's _refuse_unrecognised_keys, so the 509 class of dropped keys recurs. The 312 bound was fixed in one decoder only (web-form-parsing.3 (fk-9dd1d9389dd2)). Every fix to fleet_config.py (512, 519, 535, 561) patched one shape. The distribution types are not in __all__ (verified), so a public seam here is free of the frozen contract.
chains.proposal: Expose a narrow seam in config, or in the extracted fleet_distribution.py once chain 1's primitives sit below it: parse_distribution_spec(data, path) and draw_values(spec, n, seed), the latter wrapping _DistributionSampler. Ideally give each frozen distribution type a sample(rng) method. Make the editor distribution the single wire shape, with one decoder to and from config's grammar, iterating FLEET_COMPONENTS.grammar_key. The web layer passes blocks through unchanged so config's key and presence rules see what the user posted. The builder imports and saves presets through a shared server importer that returns {form, not_loaded}. This deletes _draw_samples, _build_distribution_dict, _spec_number, _pool_counts, builder_form's prefixed decoder, the page scripts' serialisers and the builder's js-yaml import path. Depends on chain 1 for the number rule.

chains.name: A component's field list and defaults are restated in up to seven places (dataclass, reader key set, distribution config, sampler fallbacks, sweep rebuilders, writer), and some fields have no consumer at all
chains.description: Defect: no single declaration of which component fields the scenario grammar expresses. Evidence across clusters: PVConfig.system_losses is in neither _PV_BLOCK_KEYS nor scenario_writer._pv_block (spot-checked: no system_losses in scenario_writer.py), so it round-trips silently to 0.1408 (scenario-config.4 (fk-2b16cc8bcf46), pv-weather.4 (fk-d2b4045c6676)). _modify_pv_config and _modify_battery_config drop different subsets (f5c5356; live 237, 320), and scenario-config.7 (fk-59fdc80fdded) shows run_parameter_sweep, their only caller, has no production caller. Defaults are restated four times per component (live 599, 600). The PV-weather side runs the other way. module_efficiency is sampled per home by generate_homes_from_distribution but read nowhere in pv.py, and temperature_coefficient applies only through a `!= -0.004` sentinel (pv-weather.1 (fk-0edf0069c6bb), live 195; same shape as 236). _module_rating_w's 400 W fallback (pv-weather.7 (fk-a98db49f3fd7)) is the same 'field present, not what the model reads' gap. The config cluster saw 'fields restated'; the PV cluster saw 'fields not consumed'. Together they are one defect: no table ties a field to its reader, its writer and its consumer.
chains.proposal: Delete run_parameter_sweep, _apply_parameter_to_home, the three _modify_* functions, ParameterSweepConfig and SweepResult (none is in __all__), and close 237 and 320 as obsolete. Declare one field-to-reader table per component, keyed by dataclass field. It drives the block reader (chain 1's read_block), the writer and the distribution's recognised keys. The sampler builds Cls(**non-None sampled) so dataclass defaults apply. A parametrised test asserts dataclasses.fields(Cls) == table keys plus a reviewed set of non-grammar fields. For PV, settle the module spec (pv-weather.1 (fk-0edf0069c6bb)): either wire module_efficiency and temperature_coefficient (gamma_r) into the CEC path with a measurement, or take them out of the grammar and distributions. Removing them from PVConfig itself would need a bump; removing them from the grammar does not. Resolve the module rating from pdc0/STC with no 400 W default.

chains.name: A scenario document, and its scenario-level pricing and dispatch overlays, are resolved separately by each consumer (CLI commands, validate, web, finance, optimize)
chains.description: Defect: config has no typed classification of a document and no resolution of overlays at parse time. Document shape is decided by key presence in at least five places (scenario-config.3 (fk-2264bc150fa3)). `home run` mutates the raw dict, so a flat 9 kW home runs as 4 kW (live 422, 681). ScenarioConfig keeps seg and tariff_config unresolved. I verified tariff_config is parsed at config.py:2063 and no consumer of the scenario-level value was found. SEG is threaded separately by cli/finance, cli/optimize, cli/home, finance._reconcile_seg_homes and optimize._repriced_at_seg_rate (89, 185, 286, live 187, 296). Each finance entry re-resolves homes, timezone and period from ScenarioConfig, and the two age-0 simulations already diverge on battery SOH (finance-projection.4 (fk-4a9af7c31a4f)). The dispatch-routing precedence is decided in simulate_home and restated as a warning in config's fleet reader (home-battery-dispatch.4 (fk-04b52ee632c6), 340, 519). The web builder's browser importer is a sixth reader of the same document (web-form-parsing.7 (fk-40dff1473b94)). Merges: finance-projection.3 (fk-81d0840d19e2)'s resolve_scenario_pricing with scenario-config.3 (fk-2264bc150fa3)'s read_config_document are one parse-boundary owner.
chains.proposal: Add one classifier in config: read_config_document(document) -> a tagged union of frozen document types. Each type refuses top-level keys it does not read and yields HomeConfigs with seg and tariff overlays already applied, refusing conflicting per-home rates there. CLI overrides apply to parsed HomeConfigs via dataclasses.replace. Finance and optimize take a frozen ResolvedFleetRun built once, keeping ScenarioConfig-accepting wrappers for the frozen API. Dispatch precedence moves to one resolve_dispatch(home) -> DispatchPlan that config's warning calls. Deprecating ScenarioConfig.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh/tariff_config, and any new public finance parameter, are frozen-contract changes that need the deliberate bump. The classifier and resolver themselves can land first without one.

chains.name: A stored run's summary is an untyped dict whose home and fleet key sets differ, read by string at six places that bypass RunStorage
chains.description: Defect, physics side: fleet.FleetSummary names the same quantities differently from home.SummaryStatistics (fleet_self_consumption_ratio, and no battery totals). Defect, storage side: RunRecord.decoded_summary returns Any and ignores run type. The web-jobs cluster saw the list, assistant and aggregate readers return null (live 653). The templates cluster saw the compare charts draw 0 through .get(key, 0) (live 565, 654). These are one root cause from two sides, so merge web-jobs-runs.3 (fk-a37ed16d59c5) with web-templates-theme.4 (fk-3239afd8ce6b). The runs table has several writers and readers outside RunStorage: _record_new_job's restated INSERT, raw SQL in api, routes and assistant (live 468), and a 'sweep' RunType that is never written (web-jobs-runs.5 (fk-9d7f66fdcfdd)). The jobs table is write-only, and maintaining it caused 543 and 627 and the pre-try connection in live 646 (web-jobs-runs.4 (fk-c14c02dc1b77)).
chains.proposal: Make RunStorage the only SQL owner of runs and inject it into JobManager. Have RunRecord.summary() return SummaryStatistics | FleetSummary by type, and add one RunHeadline projection in the web layer as the only place fleet_* maps to the common names. History, the assistant, aggregate stats, get_job_results and the compare charts all read it. FleetSummary is not in the frozen contract (verified: not in __all__ or FROZEN_CLOSURE), so headline properties may go there. SummaryStatistics is frozen and must not gain them without a bump, so keep the mapping in RunHeadline. Delete the jobs table writes, or give the table a reader. Either write 'sweep' runs or remove 'sweep' from RunType.

chains.name: Job state and its progress stream have no single owner or wire contract: a destructive event queue, four independently written status facts, and two JS parsers
chains.description: Across server and browser: get_events drains a single-consumer deque although a job has several subscribers (live 680). That forced get_job_progress's hand-built late-subscriber frame (641, fixed just after the pin by another hand path, _FINAL_EVENT_TYPE_BY_STATUS). Frames differ by event type. The server's 'error' event collides with EventSource's transport error, so both progress-tracker.js and parameter-sweep.js mark a running job failed on a dropped connection or the timeout frame (live 648, 564). Terminality comes from _run_job's try, not from the executor boundary, so exceptions before it leave jobs 'running' (live 646). A completed run can be overwritten as failed (web-jobs-runs.2 (fk-484952247bb6)). Merges: .1 with .6 (a versioned snapshot removes both the queue and the per-type frames). .2 with web-jobs-runs.4 (fk-c14c02dc1b77) in the previous chain (the jobs table is the fourth status writer).
chains.proposal: Use one transition writer with a LEGAL_JOB_TRANSITIONS table, and have _finish_job enforce terminality from future.exception()/cancelled(). Keep a versioned JobState snapshot per job; each SSE stream holds its own cursor and emits the full asdict(JobState) under event names derived from status ('job-progress', 'job-complete', 'job-failed'), plus a distinct 'stream-closed' event with a typed reason. One static/js/job-stream.js client serves both pages and treats a transport drop as 'disconnected'. A test asserts the frame keys equal JobState's fields.

chains.name: Server facts reach page scripts and templates by literal copy: bounds, sweep ranges, palette, chart ids and status colours
chains.description: The web-form cluster found MAX_FLEET_HOMES as 500 in fleet.html, 1000 in fleet-simulator.js and 10_000 on the server. It also found the PV bound in four places and the sweep ranges disagreeing with FLEET_COMPONENTS (live 376, 612, 140, 664, 676, 522). The templates cluster found the same restatement for chart ids, titles and heights and the '{}' emptiness rule (637, 674, 639), for the palette and status colours in tailwind, charts.py, chart-renderer.js and macros (235, 343, 539, 537), and for card and tab markup bypassing macros (188, 213, 275, 385, 418). The compensating mechanism is the same in both: about eight regex and parser guard modules (web-templates-theme.7 (fk-2e7ddcee2379)) and hand-kept per-page channels (scenarios._script_components, home.html's consumptionRange). There is no one server-to-client channel for constants, and no one typed chart or panel description.
chains.proposal: Add one Flask context_processor that injects a frozen page_limits() value: fleet, seed and window maxima, FLEET_COMPONENTS ranges and defaults, the home PV range, and the sweep parameter table that SweepRequest also reads. It also injects the semantic theme tokens, exposed to JS as CSS custom properties. Templates and scripts read limits.* and the CSS variables. Client-side refusals defer to the server's answer. Results pages render from a ChartPanel list through one partial and chart_container. Tab bars and labelled controls go through macros whose signatures require labels. The guard parsers then shrink as a ratchet.

chains.name: The module-global weather cache is invisible across process and server boundaries, so fleet workers needed a parent prefetch and the non-slow e2e suite reaches live PVGIS
chains.description: pv-weather.5 (fk-06035cd76226): get_tmy_data(location, use_cache) reads the process-global _weather_cache. I verified it has no cache parameter. Task 460 was fixed in fleet.py by a parent-side prefetch. build-lanes.3 (fk-eec3806e584e): the e2e mark exempts tests from the offline guard wholesale. tests/e2e/conftest.py builds the real JobManager and never seeds a weather cache (verified: its only JobManager override is the held_simulation stub at line 156). So non-slow form-submission tests run real simulate_home against live PVGIS (live 366, 387; lane fix tasks 357, 508, 624). The build-lanes reviewer proposed stubbing simulate_home. The root cause is upstream: the cache is not an explicit input the e2e app can be given.
chains.proposal: Make the cache an explicit keyword argument of get_tmy_data, with the process default resolved only at the CLI, web and facade entry points. get/set_weather_cache stay exported as default suppliers, so no frozen signature is removed; adding the keyword is a signature change and needs a bump-batch line. The e2e app factory takes a seeded WeatherCache, built with the existing synthetic_june_weather helper, so the real simulation runs offline. Then drop 'e2e' from the guard's exempt marks and apply the mark centrally.

chains.name: The frozen-surface lock cannot see dataclass options, constant values or spelling-independent types, yet several remedies above change exactly those on frozen classes
chains.description: surface-lock.1 (fk-879e8c13f581): flipping frozen/order/eq is invisible to the lock (live 567, 668, 669), and constants are pinned by type name only. surface-lock.3 (fk-d2881616c782): the frozen text changes with `from __future__ import annotations` or quoting. surface-lock.4 (fk-dc5370224a78): the release-note obligation is prose in an assertion message only. Meanwhile other clusters propose changes to frozen-closure classes. home-battery-dispatch.4 (fk-04b52ee632c6) would freeze DispatchStrategyConfig (verified a plain mutable @dataclass in FROZEN_CLOSURE as config.DispatchStrategyConfig), which the current lock would not even register. scenario-config.6 (fk-4435376bedb3) moves GridChargeConfig/DispatchStrategyConfig. finance-projection.8 (fk-41283f42a36a) moves solve_cost_recovery_rate to a new module. Each of these needs a table edit and a release note that the lock cannot fully check today.
chains.proposal: Land NameContract first: a per-name record of kind, bases, constructor, dataclass_options, members and value_digest, with canonical evaluated spelling and an executable 'Unreleased on main' table. Then batch every bump-requiring remedy into one deliberate version: chain 2's results fields, chain 5's ScenarioConfig deprecations, the GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig moves and freeze, the finance split's module moves, and chain 9's get_tmy_data keyword. Regenerate the tables once.

top_priorities: 1. Give the number rule one domain home. Add quantities.py (absorbing whole_numbers.py) and call it from every frozen value type's __post_init__. Move ConfigurationError to a leaf errors.py and subclass ValueError; it is outside the frozen contract, so no bump. Add scenario_fields.py path-carrying readers with a single build() boundary that config's block and distribution readers use, and turn web/number_fields into an adapter. Highest payoff: it removes the largest mined fix class, about 50 tasks across the web, config, finance and dispatch themes, and the 11 cycle-breaking imports. No signature changes, only an 'Unreleased' note that NaN is now refused. Members: scenario-config.1 (fk-649851e5fc38), scenario-config.5 (fk-e2aaf2bfe651), scenario-config.6 (fk-4435376bedb3), finance-projection.6 (fk-4435376bedb3), finance-projection.7 (fk-b69968a37b36), home-battery-dispatch.1 (fk-a9c609ecb8ef), pv-weather.8 (fk-7dcdc5559d22), web-form-parsing.1 (fk-60410de6dd0a), web-form-parsing.4 (fk-bea05911eb70), web-jobs-runs.7 (fk-239274130a5a). Ship web-form-parsing.3 (fk-9dd1d9389dd2)'s bounded builder pool count in the first commit: it is a live memory-exhaustion path on POST /api/scenarios/validate.

2. Carry pricing provenance, the PV/grid battery-charge split and the SoH-derated SocEnvelope across the physics-to-consumer boundary, produced by one flow._settle. Build finance's per-home HomeLedger, with a balance invariant, on top of them. Board-facing money correctness: the £0-tariff retail billing (690), the zero-physics-export SEG loss, the grid-charge target against nominal capacity (632), the 219/271/281/307/308 ledger class, and the chart re-derivations (469, 492, 628, 645, 665). It needs a deliberate version/tag bump, because SummaryStatistics is in __all__ and SimulationResults is in FROZEN_CLOSURE. Members: finance-projection.1 (fk-52fa98174363), finance-projection.2 (fk-caeaf35c8151), web-templates-theme.3 (fk-8e109704aa24), home-battery-dispatch.2 (fk-f126b1c9cbbe), home-battery-dispatch.3 (fk-4df47ebe6a96), web-templates-theme.5 (fk-8f26d000b68d).

3. Expose config's distribution parse and draw seam publicly (the distribution types are not frozen). Make the editor distribution the one wire shape, with a single decoder that passes blocks through to config's grammar. Route the preview through config's sampler, and import scenarios for both pages through one server importer that returns {form, not_loaded}. This deletes fleet_config's grammar rebuild, _draw_samples, builder_form's prefixed decoder and the browser js-yaml importer. Members: web-form-parsing.1 (fk-60410de6dd0a), web-form-parsing.2 (fk-a6d9f3e5a7e2), web-form-parsing.5 (fk-7893b49b92c3), web-form-parsing.7 (fk-40dff1473b94), scenario-config.2 (fk-148991ab9439). Depends on priority 1.

4. Make the web job layer single-owner. RunStorage becomes the only SQL owner of runs and is injected into JobManager. RunRecord.summary() is typed by run type, with a RunHeadline projection in the web layer; FleetSummary is unfrozen, SummaryStatistics is not touched. Delete the write-only jobs table. Add a job transition table with executor-boundary terminality, and a versioned snapshot stream with typed frames and one JS client. Low to medium effort, no frozen impact. Clears live 646, 648, 564, 680, 653, 654, 565 and 468. Members: web-jobs-runs.1 (fk-7eb56fda0b1c), web-jobs-runs.2 (fk-484952247bb6), web-jobs-runs.3 (fk-a37ed16d59c5), web-jobs-runs.4 (fk-c14c02dc1b77), web-jobs-runs.5 (fk-9d7f66fdcfdd), web-jobs-runs.6 (fk-4540d657bff6), web-templates-theme.4 (fk-3239afd8ce6b).

5. Add read_config_document as the single typed classifier of scenario documents. It applies seg and tariff overlays and dispatch resolution at parse time, and CLI overrides apply to parsed HomeConfigs via dataclasses.replace. Finance and optimize take one ResolvedFleetRun. This fixes the silently dropped scenario tariff_config, the 9 kW-runs-as-4 kW home file (422, 681), and the 89/185/286/187/296 SEG threading class, and stops the two age-0 simulations diverging. The classifier needs no bump; deprecating ScenarioConfig.seg_tariff_pence_per_kwh/tariff_config and freezing DispatchStrategyConfig join the bump batch. Members: scenario-config.3 (fk-2264bc150fa3), finance-projection.3 (fk-81d0840d19e2), finance-projection.4 (fk-4a9af7c31a4f), home-battery-dispatch.4 (fk-04b52ee632c6).

6. Delete the dead run_parameter_sweep stack: _modify_*, ParameterSweepConfig and SweepResult are not in __all__, and live 237 and 320 close as obsolete. Then declare one field-to-reader table per component that drives reader, writer and distribution keys, pinned by a dataclasses.fields equality test. Settle PVConfig fields with no consumer (module_efficiency and the temperature_coefficient sentinel, live 195) and the 400 W rating fallback. This fixes the silent system_losses round-trip loss and 599/600. Members: scenario-config.7 (fk-59fdc80fdded), scenario-config.2 (fk-148991ab9439), scenario-config.4 (fk-2b16cc8bcf46), pv-weather.4 (fk-d2b4045c6676), pv-weather.1 (fk-0edf0069c6bb), pv-weather.7 (fk-a98db49f3fd7).

7. Before any bump-requiring remedy (priorities 2 and 5, the GridChargeConfig and DispatchStrategyConfig moves, the finance split), upgrade the surface lock to a per-name NameContract. It records dataclass options, constant value digests and canonical evaluated spelling, and makes the 'Unreleased on main' obligation executable. Then land the bumps as one deliberate version. Shrinking the annotation grammar to constructs the library actually uses (fail-closed preserved) is a cheap follow-on. Members: surface-lock.1 (fk-879e8c13f581), surface-lock.3 (fk-d2881616c782), surface-lock.4 (fk-dc5370224a78), surface-lock.2 (fk-ca5301a6f39f).

8. Give server facts one channel to the browser: a page_limits context_processor plus theme tokens as CSS variables. Render chart panels from a typed ChartPanel list through one partial and renderChart, with compare.html included.
